LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup, plus a preview and prediction Patrick Smith/Getty Images In the Week 10 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the New York Giants play host to the division rival Washington Commanders . New York enters this game riding high atop the NFC East, having won each of its last two games sandwiching a Week 8 bye. The Giants are surprisingly in the playoff picture in the first year of the John Harbaugh era despite losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart in Week 2. They recently turned to J.J. McCarthy in place of Jameis Winston but kept on winning. Washington climbed out of last place in the NFC East thanks to a Week 8 win over the lowly Philadelphia Eagles but still has the second-worst record in the conference. The Commanders missed an opportunity for a win the last time these two teams played by mismanaging the clock as poorly as any team ever has, and they will surely be looking to atone for that mistake here. Will the Giants keep rolling, or will the Commanders capture a rare victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Giants vs. Commanders live Date: Thursday, Nov. 12 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: MetLife Stadium (East Rutherford, New Jersey) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Giants -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Commanders have the ball The Commanders are not particularly effective either passing or running the football. They rank 21st in the NFL in net yards per pass attempt (which accounts for yards lost to sacks), and they're 23rd in designed rushing yards per carry, which eliminates scrambling from the picture. Their most effective form of offense is scrambling, where Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota have run 29 times for 274 yards — the most scramble yards in the NFL, per Tru Media. But that's not something that you can lean on down-to-down. Daniels has completed only 63.9% of his passes at an average of 6.9 yards per attempt. While he has seven passing touchdowns and has yet to be intercepted, he has a low passing success rate (43.9%, according to Tru Media), has generated explosives at only an average rate (7.8%) and has struggled on third downs (30.9%). Again, his most effective way of moving the ball has been via the scramble. The Giants are actually second in the NFL in passing success rate allowed and third in explosives per dropback, according to Tru Media. So Daniels, with his limited receiving corps in the absence of Terry McLaurin , might find it difficult to move the ball through the air. The Giants, though, have been vulnerable to opponent scrambles, allowing quarterbacks to take off downfield on a league-high 23.9% of pressured dropbacks and yielding 225 scramble yards to date. So Daniels could have some room to run. In the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt , the Commies have turned to Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler in the backfield. They have not been particularly effective on the ground, but they're each capable outlet receivers for Daniels, who has targeted backs on 14.4% of his passes, a slightly higher rate than last year (12.8%). Doing so against the Giants may not be the most advisable strategy, though, because it means testing rookie linebacker Arvell Reese in space, and Reese has been a space-eating demon so far this season. Daniels' other pass-catchers at the moment are Stefon Diggs , Antonio Williams , Van Jefferson and Chig Okonkwo. The Giants have been good at limiting tight ends over the middle (there's Reese showing up again), so the passing game might run through the perimeter receivers, who will face off with an improved Deonte Banks and the recently-extended Greg Newsome II on the outside. Look for Daniels to at least try to test those guys deep down the field, given he has the seventh-highest deep throw rate among qualified quarterbacks. The Giants have faced deep passes at essentially an average rate so far this season, and they've been excellent at defending them, checking in second in EPA per dropback on those plays. Still, dinking and dunking hasn't been all that effective for Daniels and the Commanders, so they're going to have to try to hit on a few big plays. When the Giants have the ball The Giants turned to J.J. McCarthy as their quarterback in garbage time of their loss to the Saints back in Week 6, and they have stuck with him over the last two games. They've been a somewhat unusual offense with McCarthy under center. McCarthy himself has not been efficient on a down-to-down basis. He's completed only 63.2% of his passes, and he has one touchdown pass and one interception. He checks in 31st in success rate among 37 quarterbacks with at least 75 dropbacks this season, according to Tru Media. But McCarthy is averaging 9.1 (!!!!) yards per attempt, and he's 15th among the same group of 37 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. That's because when he does complete passes, they're basically all going for big gains in big situations. He's throwing the ball farther downfield than anyone in the league (10.6-yard average depth of target), and he's leading the NFL in explosive plays per dropback at 16.0%, per Tru Media. The Commanders' defense is essentially the opposite of what McCarthy has done so far. They yield a high passing success rate (21st in the league) but a low explosive rate (11th). The tension between those two poles will be interesting to watch play out on Monday night. When McCarthy drops back to pass, he is looking most often to Malik Nabers , who has been the intended receiver on 31.7% of McCarthy's throws. Malachi Fields , not Isaiah Likely , has been the secondary target, with a 20.6% target share compared to Likely's 17.5% rate. Before McCarthy took over at quarterback, Likely tied Nabers for the team lead in target share at 29.4%, compared to just 11.2% for Fields. Nabers and Fields will do most of their work against Rasul Douglas and Amik Robertson on the outside, while Likely will see a lot of rookie linebacker Sonny Styles , slot corner Mike Sainristil and safeties Jeremy Reaves and Nick Cross . The Commanders have not generated very much pressure this season (33.5% of opponent dropbacks, per Tru Media, 25th in the league), while McCarthy has been one of the league's most-pressured quarterbacks since taking over. He tends to hold the ball for a while as he looks to push it down the field. Whether the Commanders can get after him will go a long way toward determining whether he can complete any big plays. Cam Skattebo is back for the Giants in this game, and he's likely to take over the lead role from Devin Singletary , who struggled last week and is more suited to being a passing-down back. Skattebo hasn't been very effective as a rusher this season, averaging 4.3 yards per carry with a 45.9% success rate, but he had his best game of the year before sitting out last week after the bye. The Commanders have been solid against the run, yielding only 3.9 yards per carry, with below-average marks both before (1.09) and after contact (2.83). This might be a game where the Giants lean on those big plays from McCarthy. I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night. He had a huge game against Washington earlier this season, pulling down 11 of his 20 targets for 121 yards and a score. The Commanders have struggled against the pass all season long, ranking 18th in the league in passing yards allowed while also allowing the sixth-most passing scores. In the red zone, Likely has nine targets in 2026, turning those into eight catches and five touchdowns. He hasn’t missed a beat with the New York quarterback changes, finding the end zone in Weeks 1, 5, 6 and 9. Yes, he scored against Washington in the overtime matchup in Week 5, catching 11 of his 13 targets for 94 yards and two scores. The Commanders have allowed eight touchdown passes to opposing tight ends in 2026 – the second-most in the NFL. At nearly 2/1, Likely is a great bet to lead this Giants offense once again in Week 10. picks.blurb: NFL Week 10 picks, predictions: Commanders vs. Giants on TNF - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Week 10 Winners and Losers 49ers outgun Cowboys Fantasy Booms and Busts Aidan Hutchinson injury College football winners/losers NFL Week 10 picks, predictions: Commanders vs. Giants on TNF New York Giants tight end Theo Johnson (84) catches a ball by Washington Commanders cornerback Noah Igbinoghene (6), Sunday, December 14, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Jeremy Reisman · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 12:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's officially Week 10 of the NFL season, which means things are moving waayyy too fast. Thursday night features what should have been an intriguing NFC East matchup between the Washington Commanders and New York Giants, but that division has been anything but interesting this year. The 5-2-1 Giants are the only team above .500 in the division, and the Commanders are just 2-5-1. Division games are wonky and Washington has remained competitive in most of their games this year, so anything can happy on Thursday night. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Everything you need to know to catch the game Imagn Images The New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will kick off Sunday's action with a 9:30 a.m. game at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany on Sunday, Nov. 15. The Lions come into the international matchup at 6-2 and are coming off a 19-9 win over the Miami Dolphins . The victory extended their win streak to four games. Detroit's 6-2 record is strong, but because the NFC North is so good, they are currently narrowly in second place in the division, tied record-wise with the Minnesota Vikings . The Patriots story is a bit different, coming off a bad loss to the Green Bay Packers . In the 45-27 defeat, quarterback Drake Maye threw three interceptions, tying him with winless Los Angeles Chargers QB Justin Herbert for most picks in the league (11). The Patriots are 2-2 in their last four games and sit in second place in the AFC East. Both teams can make big plays, but it's what happens between those big gains that may determine the winner of this matchup between two coaches, Mike Vrabel and Dan Campbell, who tend to be aggressive in their play-calling. Lions vs. Patriots need to know Injuries: The Patriots will be without CB Carlton Davis III (knee), C/G Ben Brown (knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) this week and nine other players are questionable, including WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and S Kevin Byard III (chest). Brown, who has missed the last two weeks and was IR earlier this season, returned to practice this week in a limited capacity. Brown's production in the three games he did play didn't live up to his hype, drawing criticism from fans. If he can play, all eyes will be on him, especially with the team having fewer options in the run game. Defenses: The Lions' defense has improved over the last few weeks, allowing 15.5 points per game in its last four matchups, after being near the bottom of the league in many categories, including yards allowed per game (423.8) in the first four weeks. The Patriots defense got embarrassed last week, with arguably Christian Gonzalez's worst game of his career. New England's defense has allowed the eighth most passing yards per game (231.9). The team does significantly better against the run, landing eighth-best (96.7), right behind the Lions' run defense (94.1). The Lions offense is top 10 in the league, thanks to Jaymyr Gibbs, who already has 847 yards on the ground and will present a challenge for the Patriots. The Lions' pass defense is still at the bottom in terms of yards allowed (260.9), and with the Patriots needing to improve and establish their air game, this would be the chance to try and expose Detroit's weakness. Pass game: The Patriots' passing game pales in comparison to their Week 10 opponent's. Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown has 61 receptions for 657 receiving yards, more than the Patriots' top two WRs ( DeMario Douglas , Efton Chism III ) combined. The lack of production is in part due to struggles from quarterback Drake Maye and the absence of a true WR1, with Brown missing most games and the loss of Kayshon Boutte this offseason. St. Brown's mom is from Germany and it will be the first game he plays on German soil, which should only increase his excitement and production. International history: This marks the sixth regular-season game to be held in Germany and the third played in Munich. It marks the final European game of the season. The NFL traveled to Germany last season as well, when the Colts and Falcons met in November at the Olympic Stadium. MUNICH (AP) — Heading into international games, NFL coaches typically talk up the niceties of “growing the game” globally. The New England Patriots (5-4) have lost two of their past three games and have a slew of injury concerns, including running back Rhamondre Stevenson. The Detroit Lions, even with a 6-2 record and four straight victories, are trying to keep pace in the tight NFC North . Sunday's game in Munich is a big one for both teams. Lions coach Dan Campbell wasn't focused on the international implications. “Well, if I’m being honest, I just haven’t thought that far into it. I’m like, ‘We’ve got to get prepared,’” Campbell said. The Patriots were embarrassed at home by the Green Bay Packers last week, losing 45-27 , with Drake Maye throwing three interceptions and the secondary struggling to contain the Packers passing game. Campbell expects a much-improved New England team on Sunday. “You look at the totality of what this team is capable of, the firepower they have, and they’re a good team. They’re dangerous,” he said. “And they’re going to clean a lot of things up.” The Lions slogged through a 19-9 win over the rebuilding Miami Dolphins last week, relying on four field goals from Jake Bates. It was also just one week after a neck injury to All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell . Detroit's bye week is in the rearview mirror and after Munich the team will host Tampa Bay and then Chicago on Thanksgiving Day. “It's a good thing to be tested during the season,” Campbell said. "It really is. And to have to go through some of these tough stretches because that’s what the playoffs are. That’s what it is. And certainly if you got to go on the road. So, that’s what this is. This is about us. This is the next obstacle we have. Told the team we’re not going to clear it. Our objective is to go through it and that’s the mindset.” Stevenson, the team's leading rusher with 399 yards on 102 carries, didn't practice Wednesday because of a knee injury. That could put second-year running back Corey Kiner in line for the bulk of the carries. “Corey has done a really nice job, but there are also some things that Corey has to be able to improve on,” coach Mike Vrabel said, citing "recognition of the pressure and then the ability to block the pressure.” The coach said “a lot of contending teams” are 5-4. “We’ve got to start putting ourselves in position to play meaningful games in January or in the middle of January,” Vrabel said. “It’s usually what happens in the National Football League; a bunch of teams get bunched up and they go in different directions, and I know the direction that we’re going to head in, and that’s going to be the one that’s forward, positive and winning.” New England (5-4) vs. Detroit (6-2) in Munich, Germany. Brown's presence in the game in Germany marked his first appearance since Week 7 . The wideout had been dealing with ankle and knee injuries that knocked him out of Weeks 8 and 9. The Patriots ' star wide receiver sustained a hamstring injury in the final minutes of the third quarter in Week 10. Brown has been ruled out for the remainder of the game, according to the team. The wideout, whom the Patriots acquired for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 first-round pick, has appeared in two full games for New England so far. He went to the blue medical tent on New England's sideline after the play and was later spotted heading back to the locker room with a team trainer. It's been mostly positive on the results front for the Kansas City Chiefs, who come into Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons sitting at a healthy 6-2 overall. Although Atlanta seems to be trending in the wrong direction, it's still in business to compete in a lackluster NFC South. Could that lead to an inspired home performance against visiting Kansas City, or will it be smooth sailing for head coach Andy Reid's group? With kickoff on the horizon, which side will come out on top today? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 10 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: The loss of Kenneth Walker impacts how the Chiefs may choose to manage this game, but it shouldn’t change the final result. Kansas City still has the advantage on both sides of the ball, even though Atlanta has punched above its weight twice this season. Ultimately, I expect the Chiefs to navigate through a relatively tough game and return home with the win. Jordan Foote: Being down Walker undoubtedly could make life more difficult for the Chiefs, but rookie Emmett Johnson's been nothing short of awesome when on the field. Look for him to leave attempts at tackles behind on Sunday afternoon and factor into a passing game that has a less-than-100% Xavier Worthy but a new addition in Josh Downs. The real intrigue, in my view, comes on the defensive side. Can Steve Spagnuolo's unit find a way to slow down running back Bijan Robinson and wideout Drake London? If so, putting the fate of the game in quarterback Michael Penix Jr.'s hands seems like a losing formula for Atlanta. It may not be as pretty and resounding as Week 9's throttling of the Jets was, but it should be another victory regardless. Joshua Schulman: Coming off a much-needed bounce-back win at home, the Chiefs will hit the road against a perplexing Falcons squad. They have defeated the 49ers at home and put up 45 points on their division rival Saints on the road, yet they were also shut out by the Buccaneers in a four-interception outing from Michael Penix Jr. Ultimately, I think this will come down to the version of Atlanta that shows up. The Falcons rank in the bottom half of the league in both rushing and passing defense, so I’m expecting Emmett Johnson to wreak havoc on the ground despite Kenneth Walker’s absence. It’ll also be Josh Downs’ first appearance in the red and gold after he was acquired via trade from the Colts. I do think the threat of Bijan Robinson and being away from home will keep this close, but I have Kansas City pulling away in a narrow finish. Tyler Brown: Nothing like a Week 9 win against the Jets to trick the mind into thinking Kansas City turned the corner after an explosive second half, but that might be what happened. Setting aside the Harrison Butker and Josh Simmons drama, the Chiefs looked like an inspired team led by their old faithful stars. Travis Kelce and Chris Jones both posted big performances, and Rashee Rice and George Karlaftis are becoming key cogs in their respective units. A mid-season acquisition like Josh Downs can also provide a shot in the arm for a team. This game will be won in the trenches. Atlanta has Robinson, the NFL’s leading rusher, so the Chiefs’ defensive line and linebackers will need a big day to contain him. If they do, Penix, the worst quarterback in the league when facing pressure, will be forced to beat them. On the other side, Walker’s injury leaves the Chiefs’ rushing attack in question. With Kahlil Benson and Josh Ezeudu starting at tackle, the Chiefs will need a big day from Johnson. I think they get it done, kicking the Falcons while they’re down in the same week they traded away their best center and safety. Don’t get me wrong, Atlanta has a lot to play for, just a half-game back in a weak NFC South despite being 3-6. They are getting further and further away from their wins over the 6-3 Packers and 7-1 49ers, however. Published 17 hours ago JORDAN FOOTE Jordan Foote covers the Kansas City Chiefs for Chiefs On SI. Atlanta has lost four of its last five games and is coming off a disappointing performance against the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid. Now, the Falcons will have to find a way to slow down another talented quarterback while dealing with significant changes to their own roster. Kansas City will enter the matchup without running back Kenneth Walker III , which could make things more manageable for Atlanta’s struggling defense. However, Mahomes and Travis Kelce remain major threats, and the Chiefs have plenty of weapons to exploit the Falcons’ defensive weaknesses and deficiencies. How will the game play out? The FalconsSI staff delivers its weekly predictions. Scott Kennedy (4-5) The Falcons have had some frustrating games this year, suffering through two weeks of Cooper Rush and a monsoon in Tampa, for example. But last week in Madrid was different. The Cincinnati Bengals simply showed the Falcons aren't good enough this year. Their defense has been patched together with duct tape and one-year contracts, and it simply couldn't hold up against Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins. General manager Ian Cunningham saw the same thing we did, and rather than deluding himself into thinking 3-6 in a weak NFC South was good enough, he sold at the trade deadline. Now Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce come to Mercedes-Benz Stadium, and the Falcons are without All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III after trading him to the Jaguars. Mahomes and the Chiefs aren't as explosive as the Bengals, but, well, they're still Mahomes and the Chiefs... and they're better on defense. We'll see if Michael Penix Jr. and the offense can play well enough to take another step towards feeling good about Penix in 2027, but the Falcons are staring 3-7 in the face. Prediction: Chiefs 31, Falcons 17 Gerald Thomas, III (4-5) The notion of the Falcons playing up to the competition is fading away. Plus, there’s a belief that Atlanta is now playing for draft positioning instead of ending its playoff drought. The Chiefs present too many issues for the Falcons. We all know what Patrick Mahomes can do in the passing attack. And we all watched the Atlanta secondary struggle with Bengals playmakers in Madrid. With Kenneth Walker III out, that may soften the blow against the Falcons’ dwindling run defense . Offensively, Atlanta is looking pretty “eh.” Michael Penix Jr. has gotten off of his heater and must prove himself as the franchise quarterback against one of the top pass defenses in the league. Additionally, Kansas City is top-10 at stopping the run and will likely stack boxes to stonewall Bijan Robinson as the Falcons deal with the key loss of powerback Brian Robinson Jr. Atlanta is looking at a third consecutive loss on the road to the 2027 NFL Draft. Prediction: Chiefs 34, Falcons 21 Garrett Chapman (4-5) The Falcons have lost four of their last five, and the road to snapping that skid will run through the Kansas City Chiefs. The perennial contenders will be without Kenneth Walker, but Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce are still willing and able to run wild on a reeling Falcons defense that just moved Jessie Bates. On offense, Corey Levin will be taking over at center , and he'll have a pretty difficult challenge opposite him. This should be a tight game, but I'm not sure the Falcons can overcome this team opposite them right now. Prediction: Chiefs 20, Falcons 17 Darius Hayes (4-5) Expects a closer game with Walker sidelined, but Mahomes will ultimately make the difference. Atlanta’s defense has continued to struggle, and the departure of Bates doesn’t provide much confidence that things will improve against Kansas City’s passing attack. The Falcons also face questions offensively with a new starting center stepping into the lineup midway through the season. That transition could create additional problems against a talented Chiefs defense. Atlanta remains competitive, but Kansas City will pull away late to secure the victory. Prediction: Chiefs 23, Falcons 16 Jerry Jones, Falcons Podcast , (4-5) Despite being only a half game back from first place in the division, it really seems like the clock is ticking on the Falcons’ season. The performances in recent weeks and the trades the Falcons made at the deadline make this game feel like a “crap or get off the pot” moment for this team. There is hope, though. The Chiefs are good, but the Falcons have beaten better teams this year (which sounds crazy given they’ve only won three games). The blueprint for beating the Chiefs is pretty straightforward: stop the run. The issue is, the Falcons have struggled to do that, especially against inside runs, and the Chiefs are an inside-running team. If they can pull it off, the Falcons’ pass defense matches up well against the Chiefs’ passing offense on paper (even without Jessie Bates). On the other side of the ball, the Chiefs’ defense has been solid, but I think they have a real weakness in the secondary with the injury to their rookie Mansoor Delane. To exploit it, though, the Falcons will need to get the run game going. Their passing offense has been pretty ineffective when the ground game stalls. This is a game the Falcons can win... but whether they will is a different story. Prediction: Chiefs 24, Falcons 16 Final Predictions: Chiefs Are the Unanimous Pick Despite differences in the projected final scores, all five contributors are picking Kansas City to win in Week 10. The absence of Kenneth Walker could give Atlanta an opportunity to make this a more competitive matchup, but Mahomes remains the biggest difference-maker heading into Sunday. For the Falcons, the challenge will be finding a way to slow down Kansas City’s passing attack while getting enough production from Penix and the offense. Atlanta needs a win to stop its recent slide, but the consensus among our staff is that the Chiefs will leave Mercedes-Benz Stadium with another victory. Meanwhile, the Falcons have lost their last two games by a combined 33 points after upsetting the 49ers. picks.blurb: The Athletic picks Falcons to upset Chiefs in Week 10 matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Week 10 Winners and Losers 49ers outgun Cowboys Fantasy Booms and Busts Aidan Hutchinson injury College football winners/losers The Athletic picks Falcons to upset Chiefs in Week 10 matchup Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Coming off a blowout loss to the Cincinnati Bengals , the Atlanta Falcons will have to face another heavyweight AFC contender this week when they host the Kansas City Chiefs. On the bright side, the Chiefs aren't exactly playing their best ball right now, having lost two of their last three games. Then again, Kansas City is once again one of the toughest teams in the league with a healthy Patrick Mahomes back in the lineup and a brilliant run game headed by Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III. Their elite defenses is what powers this train nowadays, though. Anything can happen on Any Given Sunday - but there's a good reason why the Chiefs are favored for this matchup. However, Vic Tafur at The Athletic is predicting an upset win for the Falcons. "The Falcons beat the 49ers last month, but have looked terrible the past two weeks. The Chiefs haven't played all that well, and they are 6-2. So let's go with … the Falcons — who didn't break much of a sweat in Spain — and their pass rush, which shows up at home. Maybe the Chiefs are a little too giddy about trading for Josh Downs, who has only had one game with more than 40 yards in the past six." It can definitely happen - it's just really difficult to visualize exactly how. The winning formula for the Falcons this season has mostly been establishing an early lead, riding Bijan Robinson and then taking occasional deep play action shots with Michael Penix. The surprise victory over the 49ers flipped that script though, with Penix working a pass-happy game plan to great success. That's pretty much the only time in his career that's happened, though. Any upset scenario probably has to include heavy pressure on Mahomes, who is only human after all (mostly) and doesn't have many weapons to throw to - even after the addition of Josh Downs at wide receiver. Realistically, to win this one the Falcons are going to have to win the turnover battle. Everything else comes second. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jared Sapp · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 9:30 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Atlanta Falcons , our writers predicted the final score and result. Atlanta has been an unpredictable team both looking dominant in their trio of wins while struggling in most of their six losses. FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists the Chiefs as 3.5-point home favorites. The Falcons also have the misfortune of not coming off of a European game into their bye week. The Falcons lost 34-17 to the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, Spain on Sunday. They also sent starting safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) I do worry about the Falcons' pass rush, even if their defense's other two levels were underwhelming even before trading Bates. With the league's two best running backs facing off, I expect a run heavy day that should lead to a fast moving game. Look for the Chiefs' pass rush to build on their second half against Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix. This will be a game where Atlanta looks game for a couple of drives before the Chiefs overwhelm in route to a victory. The run game will lead to limited possessions for both sides to keep the scoring from getting out of hand. Chiefs 27, Falcons 17 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) The Chiefs and Falcons are on opposite ends of the competitive spectrum in the NFL, and this week's game should show that. The Falcons traded away veteran safety Jessie Bates to the contending Jacksonville Jaguars, while the Chiefs traded for wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts. Despite a talented core of offensive playmakers, including Bijan Robinson and Drake London, the Falcons are only 3-6, largely because their defense allows over 340 yards per game. The Falcons are -8 in the turnover-takeaway category, 30th in the NFL, while the Chiefs are tied for 9th at +4. If they can force turnovers, they will be in good shape to win the game. I don't think Downs will play more than 20 snaps this week, but I would expect the Chiefs to design a few routes for him to get his feet wet in the offense. Chiefs 27, Falcons 13 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) I've got the Chiefs winning this one. Josh Downs makes his debut, and I like Mahomes having another guy who can get open underneath, especially now that Atlanta traded away Jessie Bates. The Falcons also traded their starting center, Ryan Neuzil, so I expect Chris Jones to make life real uncomfortable up the middle. Chiefs 27, Falcons 20 Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) What impressed me most about the Chiefs' 35–12 win over the Jets was how they finished. Kansas City has a habit of letting teams it should beat hang around, and the Jets were within two points at halftime. The Chiefs outscored them 21–0 from there. Kenneth Walker III looked like the player we saw during the 5–0 start, finishing with 143 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns. To keep Walker rolling, the Chiefs need their receivers to win against man coverage. Seattle and Denver showed what happens when defenses can load the box and trust their corners to hold up one-on-one: the run slows down, and play-action loses its bite. If the receivers make Atlanta pay for that approach, Walker will have more room to run and Patrick Mahomes can get back to attacking off play-action. Against Atlanta, the key is slowing down Bijan Robinson. That's the operative phrase: slow him down. He's coming off 100 rushing yards and another 47 through the air, so Kansas City has to account for him even when he doesn't get the handoff. Drake London demands attention, and Kyle Pitts can still cause problems for the Chiefs' linebackers and safeties even in a quiet season. But if Kansas City's run defense keeps Robinson from taking over, Sack Nation can build on its five-sack performance by moving Michael Penix Jr. off his spot and forcing him past his first read. I like the Chiefs' chances when Atlanta has to win that way. Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) Your Kansas City Chiefs head to Atlanta as big favorites against the 2-6 Falcons. Yes, they've lost 4 of their last 5, but this is a dangerous opponent. Ideally, they start strong with Walker and Johnson– if the run game gets going, the Chiefs are hard to beat. The Falcons, meanwhile, are on a two game losing skid after their upset win over the previously unbeaten San Francisco 49ers. I never quite know what to make of the Falcons. They're a team with some of the best offensive weapons in the entire NFL, yet they can't ever seem to put it all together. Since Jonathan Taylor in week 2, Bijan Robinson will be the best running back the Chiefs have faced all season. The Chiefs have been great defending the run in 2026, and I think they will be able to contain Robinson, but he will still get his yards. Defensively, the Chiefs should also be able to continue the positive momentum they established last week in pressuring the quarterback and leading to mistakes by the Falcons' offense. home.headline: Taylor Swift’s husband Travis Kelce injures ankle against Falcons, returns to game
home.blurb: Kelce went to the locker room with team trainers, and the Chiefs listed him as questionable to return. A photo posted to X later showed him back on the Chiefs’ sideline with his helmet on. He returned to the game in the first half but was visibly limping. Taylor Swift’s husband, Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce , returned to the sideline with his helmet on after injuring his left ankle on the opening drive of Sunday’s game against the Atlanta Falcons. Patrick Mahomes hit Kelce for a 23-yard gain in the first quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Falcons safety DeMarcco Hellams brought Kelce down from behind, and Kelce reached for his left ankle after the tackle. He limped to the sideline, where trainers retaped the ankle before accompanying him to the locker room for further evaluation. The Chiefs had listed Kelce on their Week 10 injury report with an ankle injury. He was a full participant in practice and entered Sunday’s game without an injury designation. The team’s pregame report did not specify which ankle was injured. The catch brought Kelce to 505 receiving yards, his 13th consecutive season with at least 500. He entered Sunday with 33 catches and two touchdowns through eight games. Kelce played at least 15 games in every regular season from 2014 through 2025. He played all 17 games last season and led the Chiefs with 76 catches, 851 receiving yards and five touchdown receptions. That was his 12th straight season with at least 800 receiving yards, tying Jerry Rice for the longest such streak in NFL history. A four-time first-team All-Pro, Kelce topped 1,000 receiving yards in seven straight seasons from 2016 through 2022. He set a career high with 1,416 receiving yards in 2020, when he caught 105 passes and scored 11 touchdowns in 15 games. He and Mahomes have helped Kansas City win three Super Bowls, following the 2019, 2022 and 2023 seasons. Kelce returned for his 14th NFL season after he and Swift wed in July at Madison Square Garden in New York City. home.headline: Kansas City Chiefs HC Andy Reid's injury update after Week 10's win over Falcons spells bad news for 2024 NFL Draft pick
home.blurb: Wiley was carted to the locker room during the first quarter of the blowout win over the Falcons. The team dealt with a few more injuries as the game went on. Reid confirmed that Creed Humphrey got poked in the eye, which was clear on TV. He finished the game and will ultimately be ok. As for CB Mansoor Delane, it seems like he was pulled more so out of an abundance of caution. "He landed on his back and kind of up on that shoulder area," Reid said. "I think he was scared more than anything. He's going to be alright, though." Another injury setback for Delane's shoulder would be troubling, but he sounds like he avoided anything serious. As for Wiley, this is the type of injury that could prematurely end his Chiefs career. As a rookie out of TCU in 2024, Wiley suffered a season-ending ACL injury during practice. That injury really took away the remainder of his rookie season and limited him during the 2025 NFL season as well. It wasn't until this offseason that he felt like he was getting back to himself. However, that never really came to fruition in on-field production. Now, with the ankle fracture that will almost certainly end his season, Wiley is heading for another long rehab and recovery. A fourth-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft out of TCU, Wiley is listed at 6-foot-6 and 250 pounds. The Chiefs have appeared in 50 combined regular-season and postseason games since the start of the 2024 NFL season. Whether it has been injury or a healthy scratch, Wiley has played in 15 of 50 possible games during that timeframe. Wiley is likely slated for IR with the fractured ankle, with eight more games left in the 2026 NFL regular season. As for how the team will adapt to Wiley's loss, it likely opens a needed roster spot, with Omarr Norman-Lott slated to return soon . Kansas City has three tight ends on the 53-man roster currently, with Travis Kelce, Noah Gray, and Jake Briningstool. They have one tight end on the practice squad in the International Player Pathway Program, Thomas Odukoya. The Browns are 3-0 at home this year, but after having lost two straight games, they are being treated like an afterthought this week. As you can see in the national picks below, not a single person is picking the Browns at home. Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 10 game between the Browns and Texans: NFL.com (Various) Why Brooke picked the Texans: Even sitting at 3-5, the Texans appear to be full steam ahead toward a playoff berth with the way their offense is playing and defense is improving. C.J. Stroud has Nick Caley's unit absolutely humming now that most of his main targets are healthy. The real key to that success is Nico Collins. In the 257 snaps Collins has played this season, the Texans have averaged 8.2 yards per passing play, more than the 49ers' league-leading 7.9. He could be stalled when matched up against cornerback Denzel Ward, who's allowing 0.5 yards per coverage snap, fifth-fewest among cornerbacks (min. 150 coverage snaps). That duel is sure to be dogfight Sunday, but no matter, as I have faith in Stroud's other weapons (Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison Jr., Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson) to get it done. Houston's lone offensive weakness matches up nicely against the Browns' permeable run defense. Getting Deshaun Watson back is a boost for Cleveland, but even with him, the Browns have struggled to put together a full game, instead relying on a few big plays each week from their young stars. An all-around performance is exactly what the Browns must have to beat the current version of DeMeco Ryans' team. Thus, Cleveland will fall short of improving to 4-0 at home for the first time since the 1963 campaign, when Jim Brown led the NFL in rushing and scrimmage yards in a 14-game season. CBS Sports (Pete Prisco) – Texans 21, Browns 20 This is a big game for both teams in terms of the playoff picture. The Texans looked dominant against the Chargers last week, but this is a second straight road game. It won't matter. Their defensive front will dominate whoever plays quarterback for the Browns. But the Cleveland defense will keep them in it. CBS Sports (John Breech) – Texans 24, Browns 16 Anyway, this genuinely does feel like a game that's going to boil down to Watson vs. the Texans. Watson has been sacked more times than any other QB in the NFL this year (33), and he'll be facing a defense that leads the NFL in sacks (29). That's a recipe for disaster. There have only been three games all season where a QB has been sacked at least eight times: Two of them were Deshaun Watson (vs. Jets in Week 5 and vs. Steelers in Week 8) and the other one happened on Sunday with the Texans sacking Justin Herbert eight times. Sporting News (Vinnie Iyer) – Texans 20, Browns 17 The Texans hope to sneak back into the playoff picture and their defense got back to making big plays in Los Angeles after the bye. Cleveland's defense will get a break as Houston is one-dimensional out of necessity, but in the end, old Texans friend Deshaun Watson will be outdueled by red-hot C.J. Stroud. Sporting News (Bill Bender) – Texans 22, Browns 19 Shedeur Sanders had 297 passing yards and two TDs in his first start of the season, and that might be enough to keep that in a home start against the Texans. Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud is coming off a 384-yard, five-TD performance against the Chargers. The Browns' early-season shine is wearing off, but they are 4-0 ATS as an underdog of seven points or less. Linebacker Carson Schwesinger, who has 25 tackles the last two weeks, helps Cleveland stick around at home. Below are our Week 10 NFL staff picks:

Currently sitting at 3-5, the Texans must get back to their winning ways long-term if they plan on making a postseason push in the AFC. Right now, no one should be talking about the playoffs, especially since Houston has blown three fourth-quarter leads and remains winless at home. The good news? Sunday's matchup is on the road, a place where Houston is 3-1. The Texans will travel to Cleveland for a date with Deshaun Watson and the Browns in Week 10. Cleveland, which could be gunning for a wild-card berth under first-year coach Todd Monken, fell short on Sunday in a battle down in the bayou amid an overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints . Cleveland plans to start Watson, Houston's former franchise quarterback, but second-year passer Shedeur Sanders proved his potential by keeping the Browns alive in the Superdome. While throwing for nearly 200 yards and two touchdowns, Sanders was also sacked five times. Meanwhile, Cleveland's defense recorded five sacks, headlined by former Defensive Rookie of the Year Carson Schwesinger. "They're really good players, they're athletic and they're disruptive," Texans offensive coordinator Nick Caley said. "They've got that speed off the ball. Stroud threw for a season-high 384 yards and tied his career high in touchdown passes with five as Houston rolled past the Bolts in a 44-22 victory at SoFi Stadium. Despite a slow offensive start, Houston found a rhythm in the second quarter and never looked back. The Texans could be dealing with a multitude of injuries following Friday's practice. For the third straight day, rookie offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge did not practice. Running back Woody Marks and defensive ends Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter also could be in trouble after missing practice on Thursday and Friday. This one will be their toughest challenge yet as they welcome in one of the hottest offenses in the NFL. However, the Texans are riddled with injuries this week, which will give the Browns a chance. Cleveland gets back into the win column on Sunday with another crazy, weird, hard-fought win. Spencer German Plain and simple if the Browns want to stay on a positive playoff trajectory, they need to win this football game. 6-4 with seven games to go is a lot different than 5-5 with seven games to go, but it won't be easy against a Texans team that has seemingly found itself in recent weeks. away.blurb: Something that immediately sticks out from the Texans' Thursday injury report that wasn't present on their previous one: both Marks and Harrison Jr. were DNP in practice with their respective issues. In the event both were to miss out on Sunday, the Texans would be down to just two players in their running back room: veteran Dare Ogunbowale and recently-signed Emari Demercado. In Harrison Jr.'s case, he also has yet to miss a game for the Texans this season since his arrival. His only missed game of the season came back in Week 5 when he was with the Arizona Cardinals and was left to sit out knowing that a trade to send him out to Houston was imminent . Another injury to keep an eye on for someone who still practiced in limited capacity? Defensive end Danielle Hunter, who was not listed on the injury report on Wednesday, yet popped up as a late entry on Thursday with a hamstring issue. picks.blurb: Updated: Predicting Packers-Vikings Winner, Plus Final Record, Playoffs and More Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers will renew their border war against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday at Lambeau Field. It’s a critical game for both teams. The Packers remain in last place in the NFC North, even while winning five of their last six games. The Vikings have lost two consecutive games following a 6-0 start. Who will win the game? And, with this being the halfway point of the season, who will lead the team in rushing, receiving and sacks? And, ultimately, what will be the team’s final record and playoff fate? Here are our Packers-Vikings picks and midseason predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Vikings Prediction The Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins this week. It’s a huge move for the Vikings, who somehow are 6-2 despite their quarterbacks’ inability to get the ball to Justin Jefferson. Cousins has faced the Packers 10 times while with the Vikings. He topped a 110 passer rating in seven of those games. OK, but what about this season? With the Raiders, Cousins ranked fifth in passing yards, second in touchdown passes and 11th in passer rating. Plain and simple, he remains a quality starting quarterback. Initially, I had the Vikings beat the Packers 20-17. I’m perhaps guilty of overvaluing Cousins based on his stats this season and his play against Green Bay over the years, but I think he’s good enough to make the Vikings a legit contender. He’s not good enough to carry an offense, though. On Friday, the Vikings ruled out tight end T.J. Hockenson and receiver Jauan Jennings. Helped by Cousins, Hockenson caught 86 passes in 2022 and 95 passes in 2023. On Sunday, the Vikings listed receiver Jordan Addison among their inactives due to a finger injury. At full strength, few quarterbacks could match Justin Jefferson, Addison and Hockenson for a Big Three. On Sunday, Cousins will be throwing to Jefferson, receiver Tai Felton (three catches) and tight end Gavin Bartholomew (seven catches). So, let’s flip-flop the original prediction. Packers 20, Vikings 17. Bill’s Record: 7-2. Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Vikings Prediction Yes, Kirk Cousins is back, but Green Bay's defense is for real until proven otherwise. The Packers had some answers for Brian Flores' group in Week 1 until Jordan Love was snowed under by Minnesota's pressure. This time, Lambeau Field will be the X-factor as the offensive line will be able to hear Love manipulate the line of scrimmage, which will help him make one more play than Cousins, as the Packers score a big win heading into their bye week. Score: Packers 21, Vikings 17. Jacob’s Record: 6-3. Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) waits for the snap against the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What Will Be Packers’ Final Record? What Will Be Packers’ Final Record? Bill: 11-6 (Losses at home to the Vikings and Bills and at the Bears). Jacob: 12-5 (Losses at home against Buffalo and at Chicago). Where Will Packers Finish in NFC North? Bill: Last (with the same record as the Vikings but by losing the tiebreaker). Jacob: Second (Chicago wins the NFC North thanks to a win on Christmas Day at Soldier Field). Who Will Lead Packers in Sacks? Bill: Lukas Van Ness. I came up with this question in light of Micah Parsons’ presumptive return for the game against the Rams. Tucker Kraft has had a quiet season following last year’s torn ACL. It’s just part of coming off a major injury. So, while I thought about going with Parsons here, Van Ness will maintain the team lead and finish with eight sacks. Jacob: Lukas Van Ness. Van Ness has 4.5 sacks, which leads the team. His job should get a little easier with Micah Parsons' return to the lineup as he'll see less double teams. Parsons is a good bet here, as well, but has noted it may take him a while to look like himself again. The goal for the Packers is going to be to have him at his best in the postseason. Who Will Lead Packers in Rushing? Green Bay Packers running back Kaleb Johnson (26) rushes the ball against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Bill: Kaleb Johson leads the team with 172 rushing yards, just ahead of MarShawn Lloyd (149) and about double Josh Jacobs (80). Jacobs might only miss two games with his broken finger, meaning he’ll have five or six games to surge to the front. Bill: Kaleb Johson leads the team with 172 rushing yards, just ahead of MarShawn Lloyd (149) and about double Josh Jacobs (80). Jacobs might only miss two games with his broken finger, meaning he’ll have five or six games to surge to the front. Jacob: Kaleb Johnson leads the team in rushing, which is incredible considering how his season has gone to date. The guess here is that he's out of Matt LaFleur's doghouse and going to be a more focal point of Green Bay's offense in Josh Jacobs' absence. That will continue even when Jacobs returns to the lineup. Who Will Lead Packers in Receiving Yards? Bill: Christian Watson has 879 receiving yards, putting him on pace to blow past 1,650 yards. Matthew Golden has 783 receiving yards, putting him on pace to push for 1,500 yards. I’ll take Golden to surge to the lead, though. He has five consecutive games of six-plus catches and four consecutive games with 10-plus targets. The sheer volume of passes going to Golden will push him past the explosive play off Watson, especially if last week’s game signals that his drops are behind him. The big question: Can they set the combined yardage record? Jacob: Christian Watson. This might be one of the most intriguing storylines down the stretch. Watson and Golden are neck and neck in this category now, with Watson holding a slight advantage. Watson is used to playing this late in the season and has made some big plays in big games. Golden has, as well, so this will be really close as the season comes to a close, but give us Watson to go over 1,200 yards for the season and earn the team's receiving title. Will Jordan Love Lead NFL in Passing Yards? Bill: Entering Sunday, Cincinnati’s Joe Burrow leads the NFL with 298.3 passing yards per game. Jordan Love is hot on his heels with a 290.9-yard average. That’s less than a first down per game. Playing five consecutive cold-weather games down the stretch isn’t going to help Love in his pursuit. Jacob: Yes, the only way the Packers can move the ball is on the right arm of Jordan Love. There's little reason to believe that's going to change, even when the elements start turning colder. Add in some games that could be potential shootouts, like a home game against Buffalo or a road game against Chicago. That could cause Love to pile up some big numbers. How Will the Season End? Bill: With the entire NFC North earning their way into the playoff field, the last-place Packers will squeak into the postseason as the No. 7 seed. It’s obviously a familiar place for the Packers. And it’s a death sentence. The No. 7 seed has to play at the No. 2 seed. If the No. 7 pulls off an upset, it will have to play at the No. 1 seed. So, let’s roll with the Packers upsetting the rival Bears in the wild-card round but meeting their maker against the playoff-rival 49ers in the divisional round. Jacob: The Packers will earn the NFC's fifth seed and have a date with the NFC South-winning Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the first round of the playoffs. A big game from Jordan Love and Christian Watson, coupled with a suffocating defensive performance in which Micah Parsons will collect three sacks and a forced fumble against Baker Mayfield, will give the team its first playoff win since 2023. They will follow that by avenging last year's loss in the playoffs to the Chicago Bears by knocking them out at Soldier Field in the divisional round on a game-winning field goal from Trey Smack. That sends them to San Francisco, a house of horrors, for the NFC Championship Game, where the season ultimately will end with Brock Purdy leading a late touchdown drive to send the Packers into an offseason short of the Super Bowl. No team has ever blitzed as much as this year's Vikings, and they have blitzed Packers QB Jordan Love with even greater frequency. Now, the two teams will conclude their regular-season series with a chilly match at Lambeau Field. Vikings fans are still riding the excitement from a major adrenaline injection early this week as the team reacquired quarterback Kirk Cousins via trade with the Las Vegas Raiders. What once looked like a potential beatdown in Green Bay now looks like a massive opportunity for the Vikings to end a two-game losing streak and sweep their biggest rival. There’s still a lot up in the air, especially since head coach Kevin O’Connell hasn't technically named Cousins the starter yet. But let’s be real: Cousins is starting unless there's a major setback . So, let’s dive into some predictions for Sunday, assuming “Kirko Chainz” makes his triumphant return. 1. Justin Jefferson returns to form (for real this time) Frick it, Justin Jefferson is down there somewhere. There is perhaps no larger beneficiary of the Cousins’ reunion tour than Jefferson. The seventh-year wide receiver is on pace to have the worst year of his career after poor QB play wrecked his 2025 campaign. Needless to say, it’s time for Jefferson to reclaim his spot on the wide receiver throne. Jefferson’s 98.9 receiving yards per game with Cousins far surpasses his 65 ypg average through six full games this season. Cousins’ mission on Sunday is simple: feed Jefferson. I’m predicting Jefferson will have a vintage performance with over 150 receiving yards and at least one touchdown. #Vikings QB Kirk Cousins says he saw Justin Jefferson today, and is excited to play with him again: “You don’t go chasing things, but you understand the player he is, and you go where your reads take you. Minnesota has held two of the league's best offenses, Detroit and Buffalo, to 19 and 23 points, respectively. While many had assumed star pass rusher Micah Parsons would be back by now, the Vikings have the distinct advantage of avoiding him in both regular-season matchups. Two of these teams will miss the playoffs pic.twitter.com/7VewNM4oiT With a reenergized offense, a motivated Cousins returning to the scene of a career-altering injury, and O’Connell in “prove it” mode, I think we finally see a well-rounded 2026 Vikings squad in action. My Vikings vs. Packers prediction and NFL picks say Kirk Cousins' emergency return to Minnesota won't be enough to survive an NFC North clash at Lambeau Field, where Tucker Kraft and Savion Williams are primed to power a Green Bay victory. "Cap'n Kirk is coming back!" was the immediate text sent to family when news broke that veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins was traded back to the Minnesota Vikings earlier this week. It was an emergency move to rescue a floundering offense wasting Brian Flores' dominant defense. Here are my expert NFL best bets ahead of Sunday's 1 p.m. ET kickoff on FOX. TOP PICK Vikings vs Packers prediction today: Packers moneyline The move to bring back Kirk Cousins is an upgrade for the Minnesota Vikings offense, but a half-cooked Cousins isn't going to be enough at Lambeau Field. Not with the tread wearing thin on this Minnesota defense. The Vikings' stop unit is playing on a short week after logging more than 42 minutes of work in Monday's loss to the Bills. Minnesota has spent an average of 36:41 on the field over the last three weeks , and the wear and tear is starting to show. Linebackers Blake Cashman (concussion) and Kyle Van Noy (calf) run the risk of missing Week 10. The Green Bay Packers are a long way removed from the team that lost to the Vikings in Week 1. Green Bay has been one of the best two-way teams since Week 6, ranking Top 10 in both EPA per play and EPA allowed in that span. There are some injury concerns for the Cheeseheads, which is why I'm going with the outright price and not laying -3.5. Vikings vs Packers combo The Cousins deal doesn't do much for me, and only offers better return on the Packers' moneyline at home. This Vikings stop unit is great, but it's possibly down some key guys and playing on a short week after logging major minutes on MNF. Tucker Kraft had a nice day against the Vikings in Week 1 and has been a red zone threat in recent weeks, with two TDs in his last three games. Savion Williams could be just what the Packers need to bust this Vikings defense. The burly slot receiver is a quick hitter who can pick up yards after the catch. Kraft does his best work against zone coverage — which is something Brian Flores utilizes almost exclusively — and may catch a break if Cashman sits, as he's Minnesota's top coverage linebacker. "We're going to continue to try to find ways to get him the ball," LaFleur told the media. "You just see the power that he has." picks.blurb: Three Last-Minute Packers vs. Vikings Predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Week 10 Winners and Losers 49ers outgun Cowboys Fantasy Booms and Busts Aidan Hutchinson injury College football winners/losers Three Last-Minute Packers vs. Vikings Predictions (IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect) Jordon Lawrenz · Roundtable Sports Sun, November 15, 2026 at 2:10 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers are set to host the Minnesota Vikings in what is easily the biggest game of the season up to this point. After getting embarrassed in Week 1 by the Vikings, this is a revenge game for a Packers team that is 5-1 in their last six games. Minnesota recently traded for Kirk Cousins, so that's been one of the key talking points going into this one. Green Bay is a bit banged up , but so is every team at this point in the season. For the second time this year, the Vikings are able to avoid Micah Parsons, though Minnesota is out a pair of key players themselves. Cousins has thrown an interception in five of the nine games he's played this year. His season began with a two-interception game against the Miami Dolphins, and he's fresh off a three-interception contest in San Francisco. This Packers defense has been on an absolute tear, and even with Xavier McKinney being questionable, there are more than enough playmakers who can capitalize on the 38-year-old's return to the Vikings. There could be a few reasons for why this happens, but Green Bay needs a big game from Kaleb Johnson. Johnson looked great in Week 9 when Josh Jacobs broke his finger, and if there was ever a time to get the run game going, it's against this Vikings defense. Sure, Love is coming off a monstrous 372-yard performance, but Minnesota isn't about to let him throw for nearly 400 yards again. Love has thrown for 300+ yards four times this season. He's finished with at least 274 passing yards in each of his last five games. Obviously, Packers fans will try to go against this prediction as he threw for 387 yards in Week 1, but Minnesota's defense has only gotten better since that point. Lambeau Field is going to be in for a treat on Sunday, Nov. 15. The NFC North has proven it's the best division in all of football, and Matt LaFleur's squad is going to go all out with a bye next weekend. Trey Smack has had his fair share of struggles this season, but he's also been locked in throughout a few key moments. In all likelihood, this will be a close game that comes down to the wire, so every point matters, and there's a real chance the Packers could give Smack a chance to win the game.

away.headline: Minnesota Vikings Get Instant Return From Kirk Cousins at Lambeau Field
away.blurb: – Minnesota defensive coordinator Brian Flores’ unit overwhelmed Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love early, recording five sacks and eight quarterback hits in the first half. The defense allowed one touchdown drive, giving Cousins room to settle into his return. The Minnesota Vikings did not have much time to ease Kirk Cousins back into the lineup. Acquired from the Las Vegas Raiders on Nov. 10, Cousins made his first start for Minnesota since 2023 five days later and delivered a 30-10 road win over the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Cousins completed 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. His defining sequence came with Green Bay pressing in the third quarter, when he went 8-for-8 for 68 yards on a drive capped by a 20-yard touchdown pass to Minnesota tight end Gavin Bartholomew. Locked On Vikings host Luke Braun framed the result as early validation of Minnesota’s decision to bring Cousins back. Braun said the Vikings needed competent offense to pair with a defense and special teams group that had already carried much of the club’s success, and he saw that standard met in Green Bay. Cousins supplied more than a game-manager performance. He hit Minnesota wide receiver Myles Price for a 38-yard touchdown on third-and-23 late in the first quarter, then helped the Vikings close the game with the fourth-quarter march to Bartholomew. Minnesota converted 8 of 16 third downs after going 0 for 8 six days earlier. Braun was careful not to treat one strong start as a final verdict. He said Cousins and the Vikings must reproduce this version of the offense week after week before the team earns contender status. That is the practical test after a debut that gave Minnesota a cleaner passing operation and a season sweep of Green Bay. The result moved Minnesota to 7-2 and sent it into a Week 11 game against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City with Cousins already familiar with the system and coming off a winning first start. The trade was a short-turnaround gamble. At Lambeau, it paid off immediately. – Vikings rookie safety Jakobe Thomas forced a fumble on the kickoff after Bartholomew’s touchdown, and fellow rookie Jake Golday recovered at the Green Bay 35-yard line. home.headline: Packers list 12 players with status designations on final Week 10 injury report
home.blurb: The Green Bay Packers listed 12 players with status designations on the final Week 10 injury report, including seven players listed as questionable to play on Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings . Of the 12, three are designated to return from injury lists and are not part of the 53-man roster, so nine players -- or roughly 17 percent of the roster -- have status designations for Sunday. Edge rusher Micah Parsons, running back Josh Jacobs, center Sean Rhyan and tight end Josh Whyle were ruled out on Friday, while linebacker Zaire Franklin -- who has missed three straight games and didn't practice this week -- is doubtful to play. Parsons is still ramping up after returning to practice last week, Jacobs needs surgery on his broken finger, Rhyan will miss his third straight game with an ankle injury and Whyle is out for the second straight game due to a concussion. The seven players listed as questionable, with associated injuries: McKinney was a late add to the injury report on Friday with a foot injury. Brooks and Moore are designated to return from injured reserve but would need to be activated to the 53-man roster on Saturday to play Sunday. Van Ness and Bullard didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday with new injuries but returned in a limited capacity on Friday. Zeitler added a new injury (triceps) before Friday's practice and didn't participate. Inactives are released 90 minutes before kickoff, so we likely won't know more about the seven players listed as questionable to play until around 10:30 a.m. CT on Sunday morning. G Kevin Zeitler (ankle, triceps) Expect several roster moves on Saturday. The Packers need to activate Brooks and/or Moore to the 53 and elevate one or two players from the practice squad to the gameday roster for Week 10. But the Jaguars can't afford to focus on anything about seeding, the AFC, or their new pieces when 1 p.m. comes along. The Jaguars are set to battle a Tennessee Titans team that has played its best football of the season over the last three weeks, losing two one-score games against teams with winning records and earning their first win of the season in Week 6 on the road against the Indianapolis Colts. The Jaguars, sitting at 6-2 after back-to-back post-bye week wins, will need a road win in Nashville to keep their own momentum. That momentum got a jolt over the week with trade deadline additions of Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates III, and Davon Godchaux, but the Jaguars believe they have kept their eyes on the ball during their preparation for the week. “I think sometimes when you maybe make a player acquisition like this, and you get some star power, you get some big names and things like that, I think maybe there's a – I've seen in the past some teams that, like almost kind of, ‘Oh, okay, we're good now. And those guys will make the play.’ And I don't think that's how our building operated at all when that news broke," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said this week. "It was almost just like, ‘Alright, we know we're a good team. We know we're a good team and these players are only here to help us take it to the next level.’ But we're not going to sit back and say, ‘Okay, well, Jessie Bates will make the play or Jordan Davis and Davon, they'll make the play. We don't have to go and do it.’ I think our guys have a lot of pride in the way that they prepare, the way that they practice." How do the national predictions see this one playing out, however? We take a look below. Sports Illustrated Albert Breer: Jaguars Eva Geitheim: Jaguars Mitch Goldich: Jaguars Mike Kadlick: Jaguars Gilbert Manzano: Jaguars Conor Orr: Jaguars John Pluym: Jauars Matt Verderame: Jaguars Matt Bowen: Jaguars Mike Clay: Jaguars Jeremy Fowler: Jaguars Dan Graziano: Jaguars Kalyn Kahler: Jaguars Pamela Maldonado: Jaguars Eric Moody: Jaguars Jason Reid: Jaguars Ben Solak: Jaguars Lindsey Thiry: Jaguars Seth Wickersham: Titans Jeremy Bergman: Jaguars Brooke Cersosimo: Jaguars Gennaro Filice: Jaguars Bobby Kownack: Jaguars Dan Parr: Jaguars Joe Buscaglia: Jaguars Jon Greenberg: Jaguars Larry Holder: Jaguars Nick Kosmider: Jaguars Josh Kendal: Jaguars Austin Mock: Jaguars Jacksonville Jaguars On SI Analysis The Jaguars do not get the sweep here, earning 29 of 30 votes. Still, that is quite an easy summary of what people expect to happen in this one. The Jaguars are one of the AFC's best teams and have been the most-talked-about team of the trade deadline week after their all-in moves, though two of the three defenders they traded for will not appear against the Titans. Even without Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III on hand , the Jaguars will have a high standard on defense. The Jaguars do not like how many rushing yards they allowed to the Baltimore Ravens last week, just like they didn't like the fact that they didn't complete the shutout against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. With that in mind, they are facing a Titans team that has played much better offensively as of late. The Titans offense has flirted with being ranked in the top-half of teams in terms of both offensive EPA/Play and Success Rate after their big scoring outputs against the Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals. Cam Ward is playing better after early-season struggles, and Tony Pollard has been amongst the NFL's most productive runners over the last few weeks. This isn't the hapless Titans offense from the start of the year, even without Carnell Tate. But the Jaguars' defense simply feels like it has been hitting on all cylinders. The only quarterbacks to really have success against them this season in terms of moving the ball have been CJ Stroud and Joe Burrow, and Ward is not that. The Jaguars can't afford to treat the Titans like the Ravens a week ago, but this should still be a game that they control. On the other side of the ball, the Titans have lost their two best defenders in Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker due to trades, and the numbers have reflected it. It does not feel like their secondary should be able to keep up with the Jaguars, and I am going Jacksonville 34, Titans 12 in this one. The 6-2 Jaguars are set to travel to Nissan Stadium to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, their first game since making blockbuster trades for Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis, along with adding Davon Godchaux for a sixth-round pick. For a Jaguars team that has their eyes set on an AFC South title and a top seed in the playoffs, they are treating the Titans with the same seriousness that they treated the Indianapolis Colts and Baltimore Ravens over the last two weeks. So, how do we see the Jaguars' Week 10 battle with the Titans playing out? We break it down below. Jessie Bates Records An Interception While it certainly remains to be seen if the Jaguars will actually play any of their new defensive pieces against the Titans, I believe they will. Jakobi Meyers and Greg Newsome each played in their first games with the franchise last season after joining the team during that same week, and I think that means we see the trio make their Jaguars debuts. In the process, I think we see Bates create his first Jaguars takeaway right off the bat. Cam Ward is far from the most turnover-prone quarterback the Jaguars have played this season; that distinction goes to Daniel Jones. But he is right near the league average in interception rate, and he has made some egregious decisions with the ball over his last two seasons as a starter. This feels like the perfect week for Anthony Campanile to cook some pressure looks up to confuse Ward, and Bates is a natural playmaker. I think we see his impact right away. Parker Washington Catches 2 TDs The Titans' defense has been ... not very good against slot receivers this season. The Titans rank in the bottom-5 in the NFL against slot targets in each of the following categories: yards per play allowed, yards after the catch allowed, yards after the catch over expectation, and average seperation. The Titans have simply been a mess in the slot, even moving long-time outside cornerback Alontae Taylor to the slot despite signing him in March to play on the outside. As a result, I think this is a Parker Washington week. He is the clear No. 1 receiver in the offense, and I think he shakes off some inconsistent moments we have seen as of late and has a huge game against the Titans. Washington is due for a big performance, and I think we see it this Sunday against the Titans. Cam Ward Throws For Fewer Than 150 Yards There have been 275 quarterback performances this season. In just 39 of those performances, we have seen quarterbacks throw for fewer than 150 yards. Cam Ward makes up two of those games, a number that is trumped only by Bo Nix and Malis Willis which is, well, not great company to be in as far as productive gunslingers go. Ward has been more productive and explosive as of late and is coming off one of the best games of his career, but I predict the Jaguars limit Ward to under 150. Ward threw for just 141 yards against the Jaguars in Week 13 a year ago, and the Jaguars limited Daniel Jones and Joe Fagnano to a combined 189 yards over the last eight quarters. The Jaguars' pass defense is clicking, largely due to the work of defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile, and I believe we see it continue this week. Jaguars Limit Tony Pollard to Under 4.0 YPC Titans running back Tony Pollard has been on a tear over the last few weeks. Pollard, who has rushed for 246 yards and five touchdowns over the last two games, broke out of a mid-season skid and has been able to average over 4.0 yards per carry in every single game but two this season. While Pollard has been one of the NFL's more impressive runners over the last few weeks, I expect the Jaguars to be ready to bottle him up on Sunday. Again, I think the Jaguars will play Davis and Godchaux on Sunday. But even if they don't, I do not think the Titans have the offense to keep the Jaguars off-balance enough to run the ball on them. Teams can only run the ball on the Jaguars when the Jaguars are threatened by the early-down pass, and I do not see the Titans having much success there. Walker Little Pitches Another Shutout The Jaguars have seen Walker Little play really, really well over the last few weeks since stepping into the lineup for an injured Anton Harrison. According to NextGenStats, Little has allowed pressure on just 6.4% of his pass blocks, the fifth lowest rate in the league among left tackles (minimum 100 pass blocks). On his 109 pass blocks, his 87.2% 1-on-1 matchup rate is the highest in the league among left tackles; his 6.3% 1-on-1 pressure rate allowed is the third lowest pressure rate allowed in the league. “The experience always helps. Confidence is a heck of a thing, and I think he's the one that said it in an interview that humility helped. Where obviously he became our swing tackle, and all that guy has done is just stay the course," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Wednesday. "Like, never got up, too down. He's just very steady. I really like Walker's play demeanor, the look in his eye recently and not taking everything so seriously. He's able to have fun with it. He's out there playing a game that he loves and competes with, but he's playing at a high level right now. He's got confidence, and you can tell.” Little will mostly draw Titans pass-rusher Jacob Martin, who has had a good year. But after strong showings against the Houston Texans' pass-rush duo in London a month ago and then a dominant outing against Trey Hendrickson last week , I think Little has the edge entering Week 10. He is playing some of the best football of his career right now, and I predict it leads to another shutout. Fans wouldn't be blamed for forgetting that we've got football this coming Sunday after days on end filled with rumors and breaking news at the end of every sentence. Not only do the Titans play in Week 10, but they're hosting AFC South-rivals. The Jacksonville Jaguars, one of the most active buyers at the trade deadline, are coming to Nashville to boast their new pickups. The last time Tennessee faced Jacksonville, the Titans lost 41-7 at the very end of the 2025 season. Cam Ward missed the majority of that game after exiting early with a shoulder injury, and his healthy showing tomorrow is the key to a potential Titans upset. Will: Cam Ward stays hot in Carnell Tate's return Ward nearly led Tennessee to a victory over the (now) 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. The Titans falling short 36-43 in overtime was partly due to Ward taking a costly sack late in regulation, but the QB can't at all be blamed for losing a game he kept Tennessee in. With WR1 Carnell Tate trending toward a return, Ward should have all of his weapons in place to put up another promising game. The Titans even kept RB Tony Pollard at the deadline for Ward's own sake. Again, Jacksonville bulked up at the deadline - their defense specifically - but Tennessee leaving the offense untouched said loud and clear that this franchise believes in Ward. With a newly-gutted defense, the Titans will be relying on Ward to try and secure the win. Won't: Jaguars' overhauled defense clicks immediately Directly opposing Ward is that new-look Jags defense. In addition to adding All-Pro S Jessie Bates III, Jacksonville also acquired defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux.
