picks.headline: Prediction For Jaguars’ Week 10 Showdown with the Tennessee Titans
picks.blurb: Prediction For Jaguars’ Week 10 Showdown with the Tennessee Titans - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Week 10 Winners and Losers 49ers outgun Cowboys Fantasy Booms and Busts Aidan Hutchinson injury College football winners/losers Prediction For Jaguars’ Week 10 Showdown with the Tennessee Titans (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Jason Klingensmith · Roundtable Sports Sun, November 15, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Jacksonville Jaguars enter their road matchup against the Tennessee Titans as 10.5-point favorites. The Jaguars are rolling at 6-2 and have been dominating their opponents all season. Jacksonville has four wins by at least 23 points this year. No other team in the league has more than one such victory. The Titans, on the other hand, are in last place in the AFC South with a 1-7 record and have (again) started to rebuild for the future. Gone are star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who is one of the best defensive players in the entire league, and safety Amani Hooker, who leads the NFL with five interceptions. Both were traded before the NFL's trade deadline this past Tuesday. Trading Simmons netted the Titans two first-round picks from the Chicago Bears , while trading Hooker (and a fifth-rounder) to the Buffalo Bills brought back a second-round pick. On paper, this game looks like a mismatch. Jacksonville is one of the NFL's elite teams, while Tennessee is one of the worst. In addition to Simmons and Hooker, the Titans will also be without five injured starters on Sunday, including top rookies WR Carnell Tate and LB Anthony Hill Jr. However, it is still a divisional matchup, which is always tough no matter each team's record. Not taking Tennessee lightly was the first of my five keys to a Jaguars victory. If Jacksonville remains as focused on the Titans as it was on the Colts and Ravens in the past two weeks, this one could get ugly quickly. If the Jaguars get caught looking ahead to next week's road tilt against the first-place New York Giants , Jacksonville could fall victim to a huge upset. Don't bet on that happening. Jacksonville's high-powered offense will be going against a Tennessee defense that ranks 31st in both total yards and passing yards allowed. The Titans give up about 382 yards per game, 258 of which come through the air. Their run defense gives up about 124 yards per game, which is still only 22nd in the NFL. Tennessee gives up 24.9 points per game, which ranks 23rd. Those numbers were all with Simmons and Hooker. Jacksonville's offense, meanwhile, is averaging about 346 yards per game, and its average of 28.6 points per contest is the fourth-most in the league. Trevor Lawrence and Co. should have a field day. Defensively, the Jaguars give up only 15.1 points per game, the second-fewest in the league. Their run defense ranks fifth at about 89 yards per game. That is after the Jaguars gave up 172 rushing yards against Baltimore last week, many of which came during garbage time of Jacksonville's 33–10 win. The Jaguars should be able to dominate for the third week in a row. Unless Jacksonville gets caught looking past the Titans, the team should easily improve to 7-2 and continue flexing its muscles as one of the NFL's top Super Bowl contenders. Given the results of Jacksonville's last two games against inferior opponents, I don't expect the Jaguars to fall victim to a trap game. Prediction: Jaguars 38, Titans 9

(Video via Jake Arthur/ColtsRoundtable) Under the current circumstances, it by no means makes sense to favor the Indianapolis Colts (2-7) in a game. They were already reeling enough to fire general manager Chris Ballard last month, then trade franchise pillars Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner the following week. Then this week, the fire sale continued as the team traded its top two active receivers, Josh Downs and Keenan Allen. However, despite the clear focus on the Colts' future rather than the present, this week's opponent, the Miami Dolphins (1-7), is in even worse shape. Three of their best players are unavailable this week, as quarterback Malik Willis and defensive tackle Zach Sieler were placed on Injured Reserve, and center Aaron Brewer is out with a concussion. Kyle McCord will be making his first-career start against a defensive coordinator in Lou Anarumo, who enjoys making things as difficult as possible for inexperienced quarterbacks. The Colts are 3.5-point favorites in this one, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , but what do the local experts think? Here is how the ColtsRoundtable staff sees Sunday's game unfolding. Jake Arthur ( @JakeArthurNFL ): Colts 24, Dolphins 10 "I'm going to give head coach Shane Steichen the benefit of the doubt and say that he uses this time as an opportunity to reimagine what the offense does. Right now, all you have is two solid runners and a bunch of pedestrian receivers whose career calling cards are centered around chunk plays. Daniel Jones is going to have to sacrifice the short-throw safety of guys like Downs and Allen and push the ball a little further to the likes of Laquon Treadwell, Ashton Dulin, and Deion Burks. "On the defensive side of the ball, the young players are actually providing something promising to watch. The defense overall isn't great, but young linemen such as Adetomiwa Adebawore, Jaylahn Tuimoloau, and Caden Curry are playing really well as of late, and rookie linebacker CJ Allen continues to improve. I think Anarumo thrives against young, inexperienced quarterbacks like McCord. Dial up the pressure." Jake on the season: 5-4 Zach Hicks ( @ZachHicks2 ): Colts 16, Dolphins 13 "This week's game between the Colts and the Dolphins has the makings of a slugfest. The Colts come into this one riding a five-game losing streak while having Treadwell as the only receiver on the roster with more than 100 snaps played this season. "Meanwhile, the Dolphins are giving McCord his first-ever start at quarterback with Willis on Injured Reserve. Points will be at a premium in this one, so I expect a low-scoring affair. The Colts narrowly get the win in my prediction but we should be in store for some ugly football this Sunday." Zach on the season: 7-2 The Colts take on the Dolphins at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis on Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS .

away.headline: Dolphins Hit With Unfortunate Aaron Brewer News in Latest Injury Report
away.blurb: The only other player who has now been hit with a DNP (did not participate) is rookie wide receiver Chris Bell. Bell is still dealing with a knee injury, which is connected to his torn ACL that he suffered at the end of his collegiate career in 2025. Bell has appeared on the injury report off and on since returning in Week 1 to play, and now he was downgraded from a limited participant on Wednesday to DNP on Thursday. Long snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder), cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. (knee ), edge Malik Herring (neck), tight end Will Kacmarek (quad/knee), and wide receiver Jared Wayne (quad) were all limited. Some good news in these listed players is that Kacmarek was upgraded to limited after missing Thursday's practice. Baker also remains limited, which could mean that he is not yet ready to play. The cornerback has made his return to practice after not playing in 2026 due to suffering a knee injury in training camp. There is still a chance that Baker could play, but the usual case is that players who remain limited likely need a week or so more to fully get back to being able to take the field. Wright has been dealing with a quad injury that led to him being ruled out in Week 9. Now, he is set to return against the Colts. Dolphins Hit With Unfortunate Aaron Brewer News in Latest Injury Report - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL College football winners/losers Dolphins Hit With Unfortunate Aaron Brewer News in Latest Injury Report (David Brytus-Imagn Images) James Brizuela · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 12, 2026 at 10:22 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Miami Dolphins have released their second injury report of Week 10, and things are not looking good for center Aaron Brewer. Brewer has now missed his second straight practice, as he is currently in concussion protoco l. It is not unlikely that he will suit up against the Indianapolis Colts. The full injury report is as follows: Running back Kaytron Allen (quad), safety Michael Taaffe (wrist), safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin), and running back Jaylen Wright (quad) were all full participants yet again. Despite the semblance of a laundry list of injured players, the Dolphins look to be in decent shape. Losing Brewer will be a huge hit to the offense, but Andrew Meyer will be there to step in. Meyer spoke on Thursday about not only learning from "the best center in the league" but also stating that he has the confidence to step in for the Miami offensive line if that is what happens. The Dolphins are looking for their second win of the season, as they will face the struggling Colts. Indianapolis may not be a pushover opponent, but they also got rid of many players at the trade deadline, leaving this to be a potential "easier" matchup for Miami.

away.headline: Miami Dolphins, Kyle McCord come up short against Indianapolis Colts
away.blurb: With Zeke Biggers out with a knee injury and Miami already missing fellow DT Zach Sieler (injured reserve), the Colts drive 63 yards mostly on the ground to take a 14-7 lead going into halftime. Boo birds already out at Lucas Oil Stadium Brewer (out with a concussion today) traveled here to Indy and is on the field with sunglasses. With Malik Willis on IR, Kyle McCord gets the start for the Dolphins, the first for the 2025 sixth-round draft pick. College football fans will remember McCord from when he led Syracuse to a win in the last game of the 2024 season that kept the Miami Hurricanes out of the ACC championship and College Football Playoff. He led the nation with 4,779 passing yards that season. Center Aaron Brewer (concussion), WR Jared Wayne (quad) and CB Darrell Baker Jr. (knee) were ruled out before the game. WR Chris Bell (knee) was listed as doubtful. Long snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder) was limited at practice Friday but did not carry an injury designation. away.blurb: “Absolutely,” he said Thursday. “That’s been a big focal point for myself. Talking to the coaching staff, everybody knows I can play. I just need to stay healthy and available. With both teams looking to turn their seasons around, the Saints will need another strong performance from quarterback Tyler Shough and their defense to secure consecutive victories for the first time this season. Here are our Saints ON SI staff predictions for Sunday's matchup between New Orleans and Carolina. Grant Chachere, Lead Writer: L 21-14 Nov 8, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints wide receiver Chris Olave (12) makes a catch with Cleveland Browns cornerback Tyson Campbell (7) defending during the fourth quarter at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect I think this will be a relatively close game for the Saints. I think this will be a relatively close game for the Saints. While the defense is flawed in some areas, New Orleans arguably has the best pass rush duo in Chase Young and Carl Granderson , who are both in the top five in sacks. However, I’m still worried about its inability to stop the run, especially when the opposing team has a solid running back. Unfortunately for the Saints, Carolina has a pretty dadgum good running back in Chuba Hubbard , who has rushed for 619 yards and reached paydirt five times this season. On top of that, the Saints’ defense will go up against a better quarterback in Bryce Young , who has thrown for 2,197 yards with 18 touchdowns and six interceptions and is the face of the fourth-best passing attack in the NFL and one that features wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan (46 receptions, 625 yards, 3 touchdowns). The good thing for the Saints is that the Panthers aren’t the greatest defense when it comes to stopping the run as they are 28th in the league in rushing yards allowed. The Saints were able to run the ball effectively last week against the Cleveland Browns , who also had a similar issue, but execution will be key. Can the Saints pull off the win and remain in first place? It’s definitely a possibility. However, I cannot trust Kellen Moore’s ability to manage and put together a game plan for four quarters because Tyler Shough and the Saints have won three games despite the offensive staff’s ineptitude. Also, add on the fact that the Saints are missing two of their starting offensive linemen on an already porous offensive line in center Erik McCoy and right tackle Taliese Fuaga , the Saints’ chances of winning decrease. Trevor Etienne will be on the field, probably taking it easy at first, the way Tyson did when coming back from a hamstring injury. The offensive line is like a deck of cards, getting shuffled again. The defense doesn't take the ball away, yet it has two of the best pass rushers in the NFL on the same team. The leading rusher is a journeyman running back who just runs downhill all the time The quarterback doesn't have the protection or running game needed, but is rated statistically as one of the best in the league. The offense cannot get going in the first quarter to save its life. On Sunday, the Saints and Panthers play for first place in the NFC South in the Superdome. Admittedly, both teams have three wins in their eight games, but first place is on the line, nonetheless. It's hard to believe, but it was just 2021 that Tampa Bay , a team tied for the bottom of this division, won it all. Point being, things change rapidly in this professional sport Americans love so much. Neither of these teams is impressive in its own right, but here we stand with the mid-season top-of-the-totem position on the line. Are the Saints finally starting to find an offensive rhythm? I mean, they did score in the first quarter against Cleveland, the first time this season they've put any points in the first period column. Is the defense poised to stop the run better? They held Cleveland to under 100 yards rushing as a team, only the second time this year, the other being against the New York Giants . Is the field goal crap shoot fixed with Charlie Smyth ? The Irishman made three of four field goals last week, missing from almost 50 yards from that pesky left hash mark. There is hope, and I am going with it. The Panthers have been on a downturn, as a rash of injuries has crippled them on both sides of the ball. However, just as everyone seemed to go down at once, they're now returning as a group. Three Panthers return from the IR this week, including receiver Xavier Legette and running back Jonathon Brooks . Mike Jackson and Will Lee III will return to the secondary after injury and play their first game for interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash. Olave, meanwhile, has more touchdowns against the Panthers than any other NFL opponent, scoring on an every-other-game basis against Carolina. Here are our staff picks and predictions for Week 10's grudge match between the New Orleans Saints and Carolina Panthers . An early lead on the NFC South title is on the line between two teams that just might be the best squads in the NFL's worst division. Getting a win is always important, but it could be crucial as the Saints look to keep their season alive and attack the back half of their schedule. Saints 25, Panthers 24 This should be a close one; we've got an overachieving Panthers team running up against a Saints team that can't figure out how to play with a lead. New Orleans has gotten the better of Bryce Young over the years and they did sweep Carolina last season but we'll have to see if that translates. If the Panthers can take advantage of a beaten-up Saints offensive line (they'll be without Pro Bowl center Erik McCoy and first-round right tackle Taliese Fuaga, with rookie fourth-round pick Jeremiah Wright starting at right guard), it'll be a long afternoon for Tyler Shough. We'll guess the return of Travis Etienne Jr. at running back and Jordyn Tyson's emergence at wide receiver makes enough of a difference to win the day. Bold prediction: This game goes to overtime, too, but Tyson comes down with the game-winning score. -- John Sigler Saints 31, Panthers 17 Despite Carolina's lofty ranking against the pass, I love the matchup in favor of the Saints. The right side of the New Orleans line is a huge concern, but I think the Saints can run the ball with some success to their left and set up some play-action shots for Tyler Shough. The Saints just have too many quality pass catchers for the Panthers, and it'll show. On defense, New Orleans has always had great success against Bryce Young. That'll continue on Sunday, with Chase Young and Carl Granderson harassing Bryce all day and hopefully a rebound performance from the New Orleans secondary. The Panthers could have some success on the ground with Chuba Hubbard, but they won't be able to keep pace with the New Orleans offense. Bold prediction: Tyler Shough gets his first 300-yard passing game since opening week, as both Chris Olave and rookie Jordyn Tyson have over 100 receiving yards. -- Bob Rose Panthers 27, Saints 20 The Saints struggle to sustain drives and Olave's big afternoon isn't enough to overcome missed opportunities. Bryce Young makes enough plays to keep Carolina ahead, forcing New Orleans to play catch-up in the second half. The Panthers get a late defensive stop to seal the win and leave the Saints searching for their first stretch of consecutive wins this season. away.blurb: New Orleans Saints running back Travis Etienne Jr. has not played since Week 3 due to a hamstring injury, and he's officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers. The Saints plan to activate RB Travis Etienne Jr. from injured reserve today, putting him in line to return to action Sunday vs. the Panthers, per source. Etienne entered the season as a potential bellcow in this offense after the Saints signed him away from the Jacksonville Jaguars in free agency. away.headline: Report: Saints to activate Travis Etienne Jr. for Week 10 vs. Panthers
away.blurb: In his first three games to start 2026 in New Orleans, Etienne rushed for 128 yards and averaged 4.3 per carry. He also had 11 receptions for 51 yards. Etienne was having his best game as a Saint in Week 3 against the Raiders, rushing for 57 yards, before going down with a hamstring injury in the third quarter. He was placed on injured reserve the following week and has missed the last five games before returning to practice this week. By the end of the week, he was practicing in full capacity and was officially listed as questionable to face Carolina on the week's final injury report. As expected, the Ringer's Tom Pelissero reports the New Orleans Saints plan to activate running back Travis Etienne Jr. from injured reserve for their game against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. The 3-5 Saints and Panthers play for sole possession of first place in the NFC South division. This will be the first action for Etienne since Week 3 back on Sept. 27 against the Raiders . Etienne, 27, was signed to a three-year contract by the Saints in free agency last offseason. He was expected to be the lead back for a New Orleans offense that ranked 28th in rushing production in 2025, the team's first year under head coach Kellen Moore. Etienne starred at Jennings High School in Louisiana before playing collegiately for the Clemson Tigers as a three-time All-American and twice ACC Offensive Player of the Year. A first round choice of the Jacksonville Jaguars in the 2021 NFL Draft, Etienne rushed for over 1,000 yards three times in four seasons between 2022 and 2025 before being signed by the Saints in free agency. Etienne is expected to share backfield duties with Audric Estime and Alvin Kamara against the Panthers. Estime is coming off 72 rushing yards last week against the Browns, a season-high for any New Orleans runner. Kamara has 157 rushing yards and an average of 3.3 per carry over seven games this season. The Saints come into Week 10 ranked 26th in rushing with an average of 95.3 yards per game and 3.8 per carry. They'll face a Panthers defense ranked 28th against the run, giving up 4.6 per rush and an average of 133.4 yards per contest. away.headline: Panthers injury report is full of reinforcements
away.blurb: The Carolina Panthers are flailing as they try to stay afloat at the top of the ever pitiful NFC South. The team has dropped three straight games with a skeleton crew of a secondary and a revolving door of players on the offensive line. The first injury report of Week 10 brings good news though. It looks like a lot of key players are soon to return. The highlight of this injury report is all of the full participation from guys that have been out for extended periods of time. Mike Jackson, Jonathon Brooks, and Xavier Legette all had their practice windows opened on Wednesday. That doesn't guarantee that they'll be active on Sunday, but it does mean they need to be activated within the next three weeks. And the fact that they all practiced in full would suggest they're all very close to getting back to live game action. The Saints are very banged up along their offensive line. Starting center Erik McCoy is out. Both starters to his left and the backup left tackle are all dealing with their own injuries, though it doesn't seem like any will miss the game this weekend. Running back Travis Etienne is back at practice, but I wouldn't be surprised if he misses the game even after a limited practice since teams tend to be very cautious with muscle injuries like that. home.headline: Report: Saints to activate Travis Etienne Jr. for Week 10 vs. Panthers
home.blurb: In his first three games to start 2026 in New Orleans, Etienne rushed for 128 yards and averaged 4.3 per carry. He also had 11 receptions for 51 yards. Etienne was having his best game as a Saint in Week 3 against the Raiders, rushing for 57 yards, before going down with a hamstring injury in the third quarter. He was placed on injured reserve the following week and has missed the last five games before returning to practice this week. By the end of the week, he was practicing in full capacity and was officially listed as questionable to face Carolina on the week's final injury report. As expected, the Ringer's Tom Pelissero reports the New Orleans Saints plan to activate running back Travis Etienne Jr. from injured reserve for their game against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. The 3-5 Saints and Panthers play for sole possession of first place in the NFC South division. This will be the first action for Etienne since Week 3 back on Sept. 27 against the Raiders . Etienne, 27, was signed to a three-year contract by the Saints in free agency last offseason. He was expected to be the lead back for a New Orleans offense that ranked 28th in rushing production in 2025, the team's first year under head coach Kellen Moore. Etienne starred at Jennings High School in Louisiana before playing collegiately for the Clemson Tigers as a three-time All-American and twice ACC Offensive Player of the Year. A first round choice of the Jacksonville Jaguars in the 2021 NFL Draft, Etienne rushed for over 1,000 yards three times in four seasons between 2022 and 2025 before being signed by the Saints in free agency. Etienne is expected to share backfield duties with Audric Estime and Alvin Kamara against the Panthers. Estime is coming off 72 rushing yards last week against the Browns, a season-high for any New Orleans runner. Kamara has 157 rushing yards and an average of 3.3 per carry over seven games this season. The Saints come into Week 10 ranked 26th in rushing with an average of 95.3 yards per game and 3.8 per carry. They'll face a Panthers defense ranked 28th against the run, giving up 4.6 per rush and an average of 133.4 yards per contest. home.headline: Saints’ biggest mistake at 2026 NFL trade deadline
home.blurb: Etienne’s return offers another option for a team that is unexpectedly competing for first place in the NFC South. However, as the Saints entered the second half of the season, they faced a major concern along their offensive line, one that general manager Mickey Loomis did not adequately address before the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday. The Saints’ biggest mistake was not pursuing an experienced center after Erik McCoy suffered another injury, especially since Atlanta made Ryan Neuzil available and eventually traded him to Baltimore. New Orleans entered the deadline with a 3-5 record following an overtime victory against Cleveland, a result that kept the team competitive in a surprisingly open division. Despite struggling during the first half of the season, the Saints’ offensive development offered reasons for optimism. Quarterback Tyler Shough had established himself as a promising contributor, while the impending return of Etienne created opportunities to bolster a disappointing rushing attack. Head coach Kellen Moore later confirmed that McCoy would miss time, although the injury was not expected to require surgery or end his season. This assessment gave the Saints reason to remain hopeful about his eventual return, but it also created an immediate problem for an offense heavily reliant on maintaining continuity. McCoy has faced several injury interruptions in the past, including a biceps issue that prematurely ended his 2025 season. His absence again leaves New Orleans searching for stability at a position that is key to identifying defensive alignments and coordinating protection assignments. The Saints have capable replacement options, but their decision not to acquire another experienced center limited their flexibility precisely when additional depth could have been valuable. The final transaction before Tuesday’s deadline highlighted that an experienced center was available at a relatively manageable price. Baltimore acquired Ryan Neuzil from the Atlanta Falcons in exchange for offensive guard Andrew Vorhees and a conditional sixth-round selection in the 2028 NFL Draft. Neuzil had started every game for Atlanta since the beginning of the 2025 season, gaining valuable experience that could have been advantageous for a team facing uncertainty at the center position. According to the Ravens, he was also ranked among the NFL’s better centers by Pro Football Focus as the second half of the season began. This combination of experience and a reasonable acquisition cost made Neuzil an appealing option for teams in need of offensive line depth. There is no confirmed evidence that New Orleans pursued Neuzil or that Atlanta would have considered an offer from Saints General Manager Mickey Loomis. The Bills have won four in a row after losing 29-26 to New England in Week 4. That’s their only loss so far this season. Meanwhile, the Jets are just 2-7, and have lost four in a row after beating the Browns at home. The Bills have won the last five meetings against the Jets, including 30-10 and 35-8 last season. Using the latest odds and analysis, here’s where I’m leaning for this Week 10 matchup with a final score prediction. Bills vs. Jets Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Bills -8.5 (-110) Jets +8.5 (-110) 50.5 (Over -115/Under -105) Line Movement: The spread hasn’t moved since the odds opened for this game, and neither has the total. You can find my best bet for this game in the Week 10 edition of the Road to 272 Bets. In this article, I'm going to break down three of my favorite player props. Let's dive into them. Bills vs. Jets Best NFL Prop Bets Odds via FanDuel Sportsbook Josh Allen UNDER 27.5 Rush Yards (-114) Geno Smith OVER 220.5 Pass Yards (-114) D.J. Moore Anytime Touchdown (+190) Josh Allen has failed back how often he takes off with his legs in recent weeks. He has gone over 30 yards just once in his last five games, and only ran for four yards against the Patriots and one yard against the Raiders. If he finds people open downfield, he doesn't see a need to take off and run, and considering he's facing the Jets' secondary this Sunday, I expect him to be content attacking them exclusively through the air. Geno Smith has had a better season than people think. He's in the top half of starting quarterbacks in adjusted EPA per play, and he's sixth in completion percentage over expected. Now he gets to face a Bills' secondary that's in the bottom half of the NFL in most pass defense metrics. That, paired with the fact that the Jets will likely be playing catch-up through the game, makes me think he'll be able to hit the OVER on his passing yards total of 220.5. I'm convinced that D.J. Moore is going to have a strong second half of the season. He's already scored two touchdowns this year, and he's averaging 15.0 yards per reception along with 47.5 yards per game. He now gets to face a Jets defense that's in the bottom five in both opponent dropback EPA and opponent dropback success rate. If the Bills score a couple of passing touchdowns, I'm willing to bet Moore will be on the receiving end of at least one of them. The Buffalo Bills sit in pole position for the AFC's No. 1 seed as they visit the 2-7 New York Jets as 7. 5-point favorites at MetLife Stadium on Nov. 15, with kickoff at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. My Bills vs. Jets predictions and NFL picks expect a shootout in East Rutherford this afternoon, with neither defense providing much resistance. TOP PICK Bills vs Jets prediction today: Over 50.5 It'll take more than a short week to impact a Buffalo Bills offense that leads the league with 386.4 yards per game and 32 points per game — and this AFC East showdown with the New York Jets provides a familiar punching bag, with Buffalo scoring 30+ points in four of the last five meetings . Behind Josh Allen and James Cook , the Bills are scoring on 67% of their red-zone trips — a rate they could improve against New York's shaky run defense. The Over has also cashed in three of Buffalo's four road games this year. But this pick is about the Jets, too. Garrett Wilson 's return will fuel the New York passing game, and Geno Smith won't shy away from throwing downfield — he's completed a pass of 40+ yards in four straight games. The Over is 3-1 in the hosts' past four contests , and I'd play this up to 56%. Bills vs Jets combo After giving up 73 points over the last two games, the Jets' defense is a gift to Over bettors, and Allen has a healthy receiving corps capable of producing big plays. Buckle up for a major mismatch when the potent Buffalo ground game ( 146.6 rushing yards per game , second in the NFL) collides with a New York run defense that allows 128 rushing yards per game, ranking in the bottom 10. That paves the way for Cook to pile up carries. He's gone over this rushing attempts line in four straight games , and the Bills could lean even more heavily on the run if they build a big lead. Look for Allen to benefit, too. With nine rushing TDs already this season, he's been unstoppable near the goal line. His scrambles to escape a dangerous Jets pass rush could also carry him into the end zone. James Cook Over 19.5 rushing attempts Josh Allen anytime TD Bills vs Jets touchdown scorer: Keon Coleman There are more mouths to feed in Buffalo's offense with DJ Moore healthy again. But neither Moore nor Khalil Shakir offers the same red-zone threat as Keon Coleman , who's hauled in three touchdown catches this year. Coleman has earned Allen's trust, drawing 15 targets in his last three games , and his 6-foot-3 frame makes him a natural target on jump balls and fades. With the Bills likely to find success on the ground against a struggling Jets defense, play-action shots downfield could also create anytime TD value for Coleman. I'd play this up to 30%. Bills vs Jets player prop: Breece Hall Over 16.5 receiving yards Breece Hall has breezed past this O/U number in three straight outings , including 26 receiving yards in Kansas City last weekend. His biggest impact may come as a receiver if New York is playing catch-up. Hall has racked up 13 catches in his four contests this season. While the Bills strengthened their secondary with the trade for Amani Hooker, the Jets' downfield threats can open up the middle of the field for Hall to do damage. I'd play this up to 18.5 and 56%. away.blurb: The Buffalo Bills (7-1) visit the New York Jets (2-7) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium, with the AFC East rivals heading in dramatically different directions. Buffalo sits three games clear of second-place New England atop the division while the Jets have lost four in a row and sit but a half-game out of the cellar in the AFC East. Working in the Jets’ favor is that Buffalo has a short turnaround after grinding out a 23-6 road victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night. It was a far more physical game than the final score suggests. The Bills managed just three points on their first six possessions, and Allen threw an early interception, but his 25-yard touchdown pass to Keleki Latu with 44 seconds remaining in the first half gave Buffalo a 10-6 advantage. From there the Bills wore down Minnesota, holding the ball for an extraordinary 42:32 and running 79 offensive plays. Cook carried 31 times for 107 yards, including a five-yard fourth-quarter touchdown, while Allen finished 21-of-31 for 234 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Buffalo’s defense was even better, limiting Minnesota to 178 total yards and nine first downs while forcing three turnovers. The Jets return home after a 35-12 loss at Kansas City. Despite an early 6-0 lead, New York’s offensive woes were impossible to ignore. Smith and co. repeatedly stalled and had to settle for four Jason Sanders field goals. The Chiefs led just 14-12 at halftime before completely controlling the second half. New York finished with only 229 yards, went 2-for-12 on third down and failed to score a touchdown, while Smith completed 18 of 32 passes for 165 yards and was sacked five times. Breece Hall returned from a five-game absence caused by a quadriceps injury and produced 87 yards from scrimmage, while rookie Omar Cooper Jr. led the Jets with eight catches for 58 yards. Seattle is coming off a quieter offensive performance against the Arizona Cardinals, but this matchup presents a chance for the Seahawks to get back on track in a big way. The Raiders have one of the worst defenses in the NFL, particularly when it comes to stopping the run. Meanwhile, rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza is preparing for his first NFL start against a Seattle defense that has been one of the toughest units in the league. I expect the Seahawks to take advantage of both matchups. Here are four bold predictions for Sunday's game. It's been a challenging rookie season for the first-round pick, who has yet to find his footing in Seattle's backfield. However, this matchup could be exactly what he needs to change the trajectory of his season. The Raiders have struggled mightily against opposing running backs, and Price should have opportunities to make an impact. With Zach Charbonnet also back in the backfield, Seattle has more options to attack Las Vegas. It is expected Price will take advantage of his opportunities and finally get that first NFL touchdown. Bold Prediction No. 3: Jaxon Smith-Njigba records 10+ catches, 125+ yards, and at least one TD Even though Seattle should have plenty of success running the football, that doesn't mean Jaxon Smith-Njigba won't have a monster afternoon. That is not the kind of production we've grown accustomed to seeing from one of the NFL's best wide receivers. I expect a much different performance against Las Vegas. The Raiders have struggled to contain opposing offenses. I think he gets back to dominating opposing secondaries. Bold Prediction No. 2: Seahawks' rushing attack finally has a monster game The Raiders are allowing a league-leading 151.2 rushing yards per game. That's an invitation for Seattle to establish its ground game and take advantage of one of the NFL's worst run defenses. Seattle averages 110 yards on the ground. The Seahawks have yet to consistently get their rushing attack going, but this is the perfect opportunity to change that. With rookie Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet back from injury, Seattle has the personnel to make life miserable for Las Vegas. It shouldn't matter who is getting the carries. I expect the Seahawks to pound the rock throughout the afternoon and finish with close to 200 rushing yards. And remember, I still expect Smith-Njigba to have a monster game through the air. Seattle could realistically finish with more than 450 total yards of offense if everything goes according to plan. Bold Prediction No. 1: Fernando Mendoza has a nightmare game in his first NFL start Welcome to the NFL, Fernando Mendoza . The rookie quarterback is getting his first opportunity to lead the Raiders after the organization made a major change at the position. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings . Unfortunately, his first start comes against a Seahawks defense that can make life extremely difficult for opposing quarterbacks. Mendoza does have some talented tight ends to work with, but Las Vegas' receiving corps is underwhelming. Seattle should be able to make things uncomfortable for the rookie, particularly if its pass rush can consistently generate pressure. It wouldn't be surprising if Mendoza throws a touchdown pass at some point. However, I expect the Raiders' offense to struggle for most of the afternoon. The prediction is that Mendoza finishes with fewer than 175 passing yards and completes less than 65% of his attempts. His first NFL start will be a difficult learning experience, and Seattle's defense will be the biggest reason why. away.headline: Week 10 Injury Report: Seahawks at Raiders
away.blurb: The Seahawks will be getting a couple of players back from injury for Sunday's game in Las Vegas, with outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu and receiver Rashid Shaheed both ready to return after missing the past two games with ankle and knee injuries, respectively. The Seahawks will still be without four players who also missed last week's game: left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), quarterback Sam Darnold (ribs/quadriceps), guard Quenton Nelson (knee) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger), all of whom were ruled out on Friday's injury report. Cross, who was able to practice Thursday on a limited basis, should be able to make it back after Seattle's Week 11 bye, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said. Quarterback Drew Lock was limited all week due to elbow and oblique injuries, as was expected coming into the week, but he has no injury designation, and the plan is still for him to make his second straight start in place of Darnold. Defensive tackle Jarran Reed , who did not practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a personal matter, was back at practice Friday and will play, Macdonald said, clarifying that it was a good personal matter. For the Raiders, defensive tackle Thomas Booker (ankle) and receiver Dont'e Thornton (back), are listed as questionable. Thursday's report featured only a couple of changes for the Seahawks, including a significant one for the offensive line, with left tackle Charles Cross , who has missed the past two games with an ankle injury, listed as limited after not practicing Wednesday. The only other changes were that tight end AJ Barner , who was a full participant Wednesday with a finger injury, has been removed from the injury report altogether, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who got a rest day on Wednesday, was a full participant. As expected, quarterback Drew Lock was limited again, as has been the plan as he prepares to start while dealing with elbow and oblique injuries. Receiver Rashid Shaheed , who is trying to make his way back from a knee injury that kept him out of two games, was a full participant for the second day in a row, while Uchenna Nwosu , who is trying to get back from an ankle injury, was limited for the second day in a row. Defensive tackle Leonard Williams , who is dealing with a stinger, was a non-participant for the second day in a row, as were quarterback Sam Darnold and left guard Quenton Nelson , both of whom have already been ruled out of Week 10 by Mike Macdonald. For the Raiders, defensive tackle Folorunso Fatukasi (shoulder, back) was upgraded from limited to full participation, while defensive tackle Thomas Booker (ankle) and offensive lineman Trey Zuhn (concussion) were limited for the second straight day. I'm also sorting out the shifting sands in the NFC West, highlighting some of my best NFL picks for Nov. 15. TOP PICK Rams vs Cardinals prediction: Under 39.5 This total has dropped a touchdown since opening last Sunday night. And it's not just the Arizona Cardinals ' QB quandary dragging the number down. Both teams will be without their WR1s, as Los Angeles Rams wideout Puka Nacua and Arizona standout Michael Wilson suffered injuries in Week 9. The cupboard is very bare for Carson Beck , with no Wilson or Kendrick Bourne to throw to, nor does he have RBs Jeremiyah Love and James Conner to help shoulder the offensive load. As for the Rams, their snake-bitten lineup is looking ahead to a much-needed bye in Week 11 . With a spread this size, I expect Los Angeles to try and get up quick and then slow things down in the second half to avoid further casualties. Los Angeles has seen a significant shift in play calling the past three games, upping its run rate from 36% in the first six outings to 48.5% during this current three-game win streak. That's slimmed the Rams' yards per play from 5.9 to 5.2 but upped their average time of possession. Rams vs Cardinals combo A lack of weapons, a rookie QB, and a Rams team trying to get to the bye week without suffering any more hurt. These are all reasons Arizona and Los Angeles stay below the total in Week 10. Blake Corum has scored a touchdown in four straight games, including a receiving TD vs. Arizona in Week 6. He'll get a lot of love in the second half, given the big spread and game script. Tyler Allgeier is now the Cardinals RB1 and is getting a ton of work, with injuries up and down this offense. He's drawn at least three targets in the past three games, and with a rookie QB under center, Allgeier will be a favorite option on short, safe throws. He's seen a spike in carries and has struck for a touchdown in each of those outings. Corum does the bulk of his damage in the second half, providing relief for RB1 Kyren Williams , with four of his five total TDs this season coming in the closing 30 minutes. His lone first-half strike was a 15-yard touchdown reception in the Week 6 upset loss to Arizona. Given the beefy spread and the game-script attached to it, Corum will continue to see touches in the final two frames on Sunday. His touchdown forecasts range from 31% to 50% in Week 10. While he didn't record a single gain on two catches in the loss to Seattle last week, Allgeier went for 30 and 44 yards in the two games prior. He caught one of two passes his way for 10 yards against Los Angeles in Week 6. Beck will use Allgeier as a safety blanket against this big bad Rams pass rush and we'll see some designed passes to the RB early on, in an attempt to get the rookie comfortable with a couple easy completions. Los Angeles just so happens to allow the most receiving yards to running backs entering Week 10, with 405 yards on 48 receptions – an average of 8.4 yards per catch by rival RBs. home.headline: Cardinals QB situation takes stunning turn with Gardner Minshew update: report
home.blurb: Following their 17-3 road loss Sunday to the Seattle Seahawks, the Arizona Cardinals received a major update on quarterback Gardner Minshew, who may have suffered a season-ending injury. On Monday evening, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Minshew “is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm.” Rapoport said Minshew suffered the injury before halftime but continued playing through it. According to Rapoport, Minshew will get additional testing done, but the injury could end his season and require a lengthy rehabilitation process. Minshew suffered the injury when he was hit by Seahawks pass rusher Dante Fowler while attempting a pass on the final play of the first half. The Cardinals quarterback grabbed his right arm after the rough hit, but continued to play. In Sunday’s game, Minshew completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards and was sacked three times by the Seahawks defense. Seattle held Arizona to just 198 total yards of offense for the game. More news: Chiefs HC Andy Reid Reveals Patrick Mahomes Injury Update Ahead of Falcons Game The devastating update arrived days after the team traded veteran starter Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. Arizona’s unfortunate situation with Minshew has led to several developments, including Adam Schefter reporting that the team signed Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice squad. This is Johnson’s 15th team in 14 seasons. According to ESPN , in an initial report on the Cardinals’ injury updates, rookie Carson Beck was expected to start on Sunday. The Cardinals drafted the former Miami Hurricanes quarterback at No. 65 in the 3rd round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Beck led his team to the College Football Playoff National Championship game, which they lost to Fernando Mendoza and the Indiana Hoosiers. The decision to draft Beck was met with mixed reviews, with many sports outlets giving the team a low grade for the pick. NFL.com’s Chad Reuter graded Arizona’s Day 2 picks, including Beck, an “A,” indicating he had “a lot of big-game experience.” However, Reuter also noted that Beck’s decision-making was too inconsistent to be a “surefire starter.” Beck appeared in the NFL Hall of Fame Game this preseason against the Carolina Panthers, throwing for 188 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s 33-30 loss. With ESPN reporting that Beck is expected to start Sunday, he’s poised to take over for a 3-6 Arizona team, unless they opt to use Johnson instead. Unfortunately, both quarterbacks could face a challenging matchup for the team’s next NFL game. The Cardinals host a Los Angeles Rams team on Sunday, Nov. 15, that has now won three straight games to improve to 5-4 for the season. The Rams also just got back the NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett, who recorded three sacks on Sunday in their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders, so Beck or Johnson could face a difficult test for his first NFL start. The Cowboys have all the talent in the world, but continue to find ways to lose games they have no business losing. Meanwhile, the 49ers are in the top spot in the NFC and should be fresh off their BYE week. You can find my best bet for this game in this week's edition of the Road to 272 Bets . In this article, I'm going to break down three of my favorite player props for this classic NFC duel. 49ers vs. Cowboys Best NFL Prop Bets Odds via FanDuel Sportsbook Javonte Williams UNDER 63.5 Rush Yards (-109) CeeDee Lamb OVER 7.5 Receptions (+102) Keenan Allen Anytime Touchdown (+300) In the Week 10 edition of the Player Prop Countdown , I ranked Javonte Williams to stay UNDER his rushing yards total of 63.5 as my No. 8 prop bet for this week's action: When talking about elite run defenses, people bring up teams like the Vikings and Seahawks, but it's the 49ers that have quietly had one of the best run defenses in football. San Francisco ranks first in opponent rush EPA while allowing the fewest yards per carry, giving up 3.3 yards per rush. With that being the case, the Cowboys would be smart to try to throw the ball against the Cowboys instead of running it with Javonte Williams. picks.blurb: 49ers vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 10 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Week 10 Winners and Losers 49ers outgun Cowboys Fantasy Booms and Busts Aidan Hutchinson injury College football winners/losers 49ers vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 10 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 10, 2026 at 11:03 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads While the San Francisco 49ers made a fairly mild move, the Dallas Cowboys didn't move the needle at the trade deadline. But these teams meet in Week 10 of the NFL season, and here are bold predictions for the contest. Entering with a record of 7-1, the 49ers sit as the No. 1 in the NFC. Meanwhile, the Cowboys are trying to fight their way back into contention in the NFC East. They have a record of 4-5. The 49ers are road favorites, but only by 3.5 points. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) 49ers QB Brock Purdy will throw for 250 yards and two TD passes It's a matter of scheme that Purdy will have success , according to ESPN. "Kyle Shanahan will have answers for both the run and pass game Sunday in Dallas," Matt Bowen wrote. "Schemed throws for Brock Purdy that create open coverage voids off play-action, plus a multiple run game with Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black to attack a Cowboys defense, allowing 5.0 YPC (third most). I like the 49ers to cover on the road." Purdy has thrown for 1,980 yards this season with 17 touchdowns and five interceptions. He has been impressive and has the eye of head coach Kyle Shanahan, according to a post on X by 95.7 TheGame via Heavy.com. "Yeah, it's been amazing," Shanahan said. "Just since the first game he got in there. That's why I struggle at the beginning of the year when everyone's asking me, can I believe how good he's playing and how much better he's improved because he was so good off the bench versus Miami in his first game and the second week… taking us to the NFC Championship as a rookie. "And I think his second year took us to the Super Bowl maybe. So Brock's been the man since he's come in, and it's pretty unbelievable deal considering where he was drafted, how he started… very fortunate to have Brock." The Cowboys will have their hands full. Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb will get 8-plus catches and 90-plus yards The Cowboys are going to get the ball to Lamb. It's their best path to having a shot at beating the 49ers. Lamb left the win over the Colts with a sigh of relief, according to dallascowboys.com. "Those are the games that you love to end up on top," Lamb said. "We understand it was the same situation that we were kind of in last week, and we didn't end up on top then, so just finishing out the game, finishing out the drive — shout out to the defense for ending the game. "But I think I had, like, three penalties alone in the second half, and a fumble. Personally, I gotta take a real good look. The numbers look crazy, but it could have been more. And I'm always thinking about what could have been. So, as for me, as a leader on this offense,I feel like I've got to be better in some realms and just end the game." The 49ers are off to a great start. But before the season, the Cowboys were in the same conversation with them. Lamb said the Cowboys need to get the job done. "We know what we got going on, just the history of that [matchup], the guys that they have over there on defense and the prep, I mean, it's going to take a lot of a lot of preparation, and a lot of execution," Lamb said. "We can't have as many flags because they have a really good offense, too." Prescott will lean heavily on Lamb if George Pickens misses another game. But even if Pickens plays, Prescott won't forget who he needs to target, early and often. 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey will get in the end zone twice Look for McCaffrey to score on the ground and with a reception. The 49ers are going to get him the ball near the goal line. One thing that helps McCaffrey's overall usage is that Shanahan is more confident that he is ready to rock after a pre-bye injury slowed him somewhat, according to ninerswire.com. "No. I actually forgot about it," Shanahan said. "He had a good bye week, and he told me before the bye week in Christian style not to worry about it at all. He'll be fine, and he looked good all week." McCaffrey hasn't had a blowout game all season. His rushing high is 75 yards, and his receiving high is 61. But he has 10 total touchdowns, with nine of them coming off the ground. And consistency has been a hallmark. McCaffrey has scored in seven straight games. In three of those contests, he scored twice. The 49ers will need to be sharp offensively. Despite the way their defense has played, they will have trouble slowing down the Cowboys' high-octane offense. McCaffrey will likely need those scores to keep his team in good business. away.blurb: Starting with that is George Pickens, who missed the Week 9 win over the Colts due to a hamstring issue. But after logging back-to-back limited sessions, it would appear he was on his way back to a return, which turned out to be right, as he practiced in full on Friday and is now off the injury report. That's a major return to the starting lineup obviously, but the storylines don't end there, so let's dive into the final injury report after the week of practice. Let's start with a man who has been a frequent addition on these lists: linebacker DeMarvion Overshown. Overshown missed Week 9 due to a flare-up in his back and a hamstring issue, but practiced in full on both Thursday and Friday after getting in a limited session on Wednesday. He's now off the injury report and is good to go, which is great news against a 49ers team with one of the best running backs in the NFL in Christian McCaffrey, and one of the best tight ends in George Kittle. So while he is healthy, he will have his work cut out for him. This entire defense will, for that matter. The Cowboys are dealing with enough injuries in the secondary, as Jalen Thompson is set to miss his seventh straight game and PJ Locke is out, too. Also, safety Juanyeh Thomas is doubtful after going from a limited session on Thursday to a Friday DNP. But none of this is the biggest deal on the back end. That honor goes to DaRon Bland, who was a surprise addition to Friday's injury report due to an ankle injury. He practiced in full on Wednesday and Thursday, yet was downgraded to limited on Friday, so it feels like his status is in real doubt, although we don't know much about what actually happened. Porter Jr. did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday, but was upgraded to a limited partipant on Friday, so he's progressing in the right direction, although he still has a ways to go before we know he's a true full go. The Dallas Cowboys are right back in striking distance for the NFC East title , as one win will give them the same amount of wins as the New York Giants through 10 weeks. So clearly, a victory on Sunday is crucial, but it won't come easy, as the Cowboys are set to host the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers. If Dallas really wants to win this matchup against a longtime rival, a good start would be getting healthy. The Cowboys have been hit with the injury bug , but the good news is that prior to this matchup, they're getting healthier--as several key players are off the injury report and are good to go. home.blurb: Starting with that is George Pickens, who missed the Week 9 win over the Colts due to a hamstring issue. But after logging back-to-back limited sessions, it would appear he was on his way back to a return, which turned out to be right, as he practiced in full on Friday and is now off the injury report. That's a major return to the starting lineup obviously, but the storylines don't end there, so let's dive into the final injury report after the week of practice. Let's start with a man who has been a frequent addition on these lists: linebacker DeMarvion Overshown. Overshown missed Week 9 due to a flare-up in his back and a hamstring issue, but practiced in full on both Thursday and Friday after getting in a limited session on Wednesday. He's now off the injury report and is good to go, which is great news against a 49ers team with one of the best running backs in the NFL in Christian McCaffrey, and one of the best tight ends in George Kittle. So while he is healthy, he will have his work cut out for him. This entire defense will, for that matter. The Cowboys are dealing with enough injuries in the secondary, as Jalen Thompson is set to miss his seventh straight game and PJ Locke is out, too. Also, safety Juanyeh Thomas is doubtful after going from a limited session on Thursday to a Friday DNP. But none of this is the biggest deal on the back end. That honor goes to DaRon Bland, who was a surprise addition to Friday's injury report due to an ankle injury. He practiced in full on Wednesday and Thursday, yet was downgraded to limited on Friday, so it feels like his status is in real doubt, although we don't know much about what actually happened. Porter Jr. did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday, but was upgraded to a limited partipant on Friday, so he's progressing in the right direction, although he still has a ways to go before we know he's a true full go. The Dallas Cowboys are right back in striking distance for the NFC East title , as one win will give them the same amount of wins as the New York Giants through 10 weeks. So clearly, a victory on Sunday is crucial, but it won't come easy, as the Cowboys are set to host the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers. If Dallas really wants to win this matchup against a longtime rival, a good start would be getting healthy. home.headline: NFL: Patrick Mahomes has a new star, Kirk Cousins' emotional story continues and Christian McCaffrey lights up the Dallas Cowboys - NFL Sunday Review
home.blurb: NFL Sunday Review - we reflect on Week 10 in the NFL as Emmett Johnson announced himself as a new star on the Kansas City Chiefs, Kirk Cousins capped a memorable return for the Minnesota Vikings and Christian McCaffrey dominated in the San Francisco 49ers' win over the Dallas Cowboys. An emotional Kirk Cousins, in his return to the Vikings at Lambeau Field: “I tore my Achilles here and it’s been a tough three years…” pic.twitter.com/8PhbEVs7Oq There are encouraging signs for Fernando Mendoza. The Raiders ushered in a new chapter this weekend as No 1 overall Draft pick Mendoza led his side out against the Seattle Seahawks in his first regular season start following Cousins' trade to the Vikings. It started strongly with a touchdown run on his opening possession before Mike Macdonald dialled the pressure up a notch on defense in the second half as the Raiders offense suffered without star weapon Brock Bowers. He went 11 of 13 for 90 yards through the air in the first half, before managing just six of 16 for 53 yards following the interval. Mendoza finished the game 17 of 29 passing for 143 yards, zero touchdowns and zero turnovers while being sacked six times. Facing the league's best defense always beckoned as a baptism of fire, so the shortage of interceptions or apparent ball security issues was a plus point. The 49ers and the Cowboys go way back as one of the NFL's most storied rivalries between two of football's most prestigious franchises. They renewed their dislike to the sight of record numbers as they combined for a series-high 86 points, with San Francisco beating Dallas 46-40 to improve to 8-1 on the season. While the 49ers flexed their offensive power, in doing so there were more glaring concerns over the Cowboys and a defense ranked third worst in yards allowed. Dak Prescott threw five touchdown passes, three to George Pickens, as the Cowboys put up 439 yards of offense, only to come out second best. Purdy produced two scoring strikes to McCaffrey and one to Deebo Samuel. Plus, how to watch, what to know, and a prediction Getty Images The 10th Sunday of the 2026 NFL regular season will conclude with the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals battling for first place in the AFC North division. Pittsburgh (6-2) currently leads the North by virtue of its Week 5 win over Cincinnati (6-2). The Steelers have won seven of the last nine games between the two teams dating back to the start of the 2022 season. The second of those two losses occurred the last time these two teams played in Cincinnati. Last October, Cincinnati won a 33-31 shootout. The Steelers won the rematch a month later in Pittsburgh. Here's how you can follow the action in real time. We've also included a breakdown and a prediction for Sunday night's showdown. Where to watch Bengals vs. Steelers live When: Sunday, Nov. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Where: Paycor Stadium -- Cincinnati, Ohio TV: NBC | Stream: fubo (try for free) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bengals -3.5, O/U 47.5 (via DraftKings ) Follow Live: Bengals vs. Steelers live blog with analysis, updates, and more Bengals vs. Steelers: Need to know Last time we met The Steelers sealed a 30-27 win when Derrick Harmon strip-sacked Joe Burrow on the Bengals' final series. Cincinnati was in field goal range when the turnover occurred. Jaylen Warren was the catalyst for Pittsburgh's win. The fifth-year veteran rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries and caught three passes for 49 yards. Warren's success helped open things up for Aaron Rodgers , who threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns with one interception. Rodgers was able to top Burrow, who threw for 282 yards and three touchdowns. Red hot teams Both Pittsburgh and Cincinnati come into this game with four-game winning streaks. The Steelers went into their Week 9 bye with a 27-6 win over the Browns . Cincinnati is coming off a 34-17 win over the Falcons in Madrid, Spain. It'll be interesting to see how much the previous week will impact Sunday night's game. The Bengals may still be feeling the effects of traveling overseas. The Steelers, meanwhile, are rested and might be getting back some key players who have missed time with injuries. One of those players is Harmon, who has missed time with a foot injury. Reasons for success Pittsburgh's success has been powered by Warren (and, to a lesser degree, fellow running back Rico Dowdle , who has played well in a complementary role since returning from his injury in Week 6) and a defense that hasn't allowed a touchdown in seven quarters. Pittsburgh is once again getting high-level play from T.J. Watt , who has already eclipsed his 2025 sack tally. Cincinnati's current winning streak has largely been the byproduct of Burrow (who leads the NFL in completion percentage and touchdown passes) and his success throwing to Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The Bengals have also received solid play from a defense that is getting big contributions from offseason acquisitions Dexter Lawrence and Boye Mafe . Prediction, pick This game will come down to two things: Pittsburgh's ability to throw the ball (which would in turn help open things up for the running game) and Cincinnati's ability to keep Burrow clean, which has at times been an issue against the Steelers. The Bengals want to make this a shootout, while the Steelers will want to play keep-away while keeping Burrow and Co. on the sideline. While Pittsburgh's plan can in theory work, its lack of depth at the receiver position might come back to haunt them on Sunday night. In close matchups like this, special teams can often make the difference. If that ends up being the case in this game, the Bengals have the advantage in Evan McPherson , who has not missed a field goal or an extra point this season. Conversely, Steelers kicker Chris Boswell has already missed field goals this season. Cincy is heavily favored to win the AFC North because of a favorable schedule down the stretch, but a loss to the Steelers would give Pittsburgh the head-to-head tiebreaker this season. Aaron Rodgers and company are coming off a bye in Week 9, and they're looking to stay hot after knocking off Cleveland (27-6) in their last matchup. Pittsburgh won a division title in the 2025 season, and new head coach Mike McCarthy has the team playing at a high level through the first half of 2026. The Steelers can get their seventh win of the year, and a few of these bold predictions might come true as well. Alex Highsmith’s Career Day It’s been a little too quiet for veteran outside linebacker Alex Highsmith. He recorded 0.5 sacks in the team’s latest win, but he hasn’t recorded an individual sack since Week 2 against the New England Patriots. His previous in-game highs are 11 tackles and 3.0 sacks. Against the Bengals this week, Highsmith breaks the tackles record and posts multiple sacks. Jaylen Warren Records Two Receiving Touchdowns Jaylen Warren is the best piece of the Steelers’ offense, and It’s undeniable. He’s one of the best running backs in the NFL this season and he’s single-handedly carried this offense at times. What he hasn’t done, however, is consistently find the endzone. He has just two rushing touchdowns and one receiving touchdown on the season, with two of his total scores coming in the same contest against the Indianapolis Colts. That changes in Week 10. Against the Bengals, I predict Warren will dominate both out of the backfield and as a receiving threat. As a receiver is where I believe he will do his most damage, finding the end zone twice on passing plays. The Bengals might have a plan to limit Warren on the ground, but that’s not enough to keep him from making an impact. away.blurb: Courtesy of Wednesday's Week 10 injury report, the Steelers saw three players, who have missed time with their respective injuries, return to practice as full participants: wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf), cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring), and cornerback Doneiko Slaughter (hamstring). Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL College football winners/losers Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals Andrew Vasquez, Steelers Wire · Steelers Wire Thu, November 12, 2026 at 3:58 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers received great injury news regarding three of their players ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengal s. Skowronek, who began his career with the Los Angeles Rams (2021–2023), also spent time with the Houston Texans (2024) before joining the Steelers in 2024. A solid wide receiver depth piece and special teams ace, Skowronek suffered his calf injury in Week 5 and has missed the past three games. Echols, who began his career with the New York Jets (2021–2024), joined the Steelers in 2025 free agency. An underrated contributor for Pittsburgh's defense last season, Echols suffered his hamstring injury during Week 6 and has missed the past two games. Slaughter, who began his NFL career with the Jacksonville Jaguars (2025), joined the Steelers on a reserve/future contract in January 2026. After a strong preseason and training camp, Slaughter was signed back to the active roster on October 10, but unfortunately suffered a hamstring injury in Week 7 and has missed the past game. The fact that Skowronek, Echols, and Slaughter were able to be full participants at Wednesday's practice gives them an excellent shot at returning in Week 10 for Sunday Night Football against the Bengals . away.headline: Steelers’ DeShon Elliott Suffers Pregame Injury, Out Against Bengals
away.blurb: Steelers’ DeShon Elliott Suffers Pregame Injury, Out Against Bengals Skip to main content SI.COM According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, safety DeShon Elliott suffered a knee injury during pregame warm-ups at Paycor Stadium and has been ruled out vs. Cincinnati as a result. Steelers S Deshon Elliott injured his knee during the pregame and has been ruled out for tonight’s game vs. Cincinnati. Elliott was listed on the injury report this week with an ankle injury, though he was a full participant on both November 12 and 13 after initially being limited on November 11, and thus was not listed with a game designation. The Pittsburgh Steelers have lost a key piece of their secondary for a monumental Week 10 showdown against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football. Having to face an explosive Bengals passing offense led by quarterback Joe Burrow as well as the star wide receiver duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins now becomes much tougher of a task for Pittsburgh without Elliott on the field. The Steelers, though, were able to at least hold Cincinnati in check to an extent during their first meeting this season, which resulted in a 30-27 victory for the black and gold at Acrisure Stadium in Week 3. Elliott was not active for that contest either, while residing on the reserve/injured list to open the year after going down with a season-ending knee/hamstring injury in Week 8 of the 2025 campaign. It's not unfamiliar territory for that trio, as Elliott has only appeared in two games and played 43 defensive snaps since being activated from IR ahead of Pittsburgh's Week 7 game against the New Orleans Saints in Paris. Holding up in coverage as a group on the back end of the defense against the likes of Chase and Higgins would've been a big ask even with Elliott on the field, though, and being down a veteran like that could have reverberating effects when facing a passing offense that averages the most yards per game (285.5) in the league. Where the Steelers' safeties shouldn't have much of an issue holding down the fort, however, is against the Bengals' run game. picks.blurb: Chargers vs. Ravens: 4 bold predictions for Week 10 matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Week 10 Winners and Losers 49ers outgun Cowboys Fantasy Booms and Busts Aidan Hutchinson injury College football winners/losers Chargers vs. Ravens: 4 bold predictions for Week 10 matchup Ricardo Sandoval , Chargers Wire · Chargers Wire Mon, November 16, 2026 at 5:51 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chargers weren't so quiet this past week during the trade deadline. After reports surfaced that they would stand pat, the Bolts made one trade. However, it was rescinded. Daiyan Henley is back with the Chargers after the trade with the Broncos fell through. After all that, the Bolts have the same team heading into Week 10 when they face the Ravens . Los Angeles is the league's only winless team. They are 0-8, but they have a great opportunity to get their first win over the hobbled Ravens. If these four things happen, the Chargers could possibly get a win. Daiyan Henley records a season-high in tackles It was a whirlwind of a week for the Chargers linebacker. First, Henley finds out he was traded from the team that drafted him four seasons ago to their division rival, the Broncos. And a little over 24 hours later, the trade fell through after a failed physical. Henley is back with the team now, and I think he will be out for blood. Last week, Henley recorded a season-high 10 tackles against the Texans . I think he set another season-high in primetime against the Ravens. Chargers keep Derrick Henry under 100 rushing yards The Chargers' run defense ranks in the bottom half in that category, allowing an average of 122 rushing yards per game. Through eight games, the Chargers have allowed 11 rushing touchdowns. Los Angeles will face their toughest test yet with running back Derrick Henry. It's been tough sledding for Henry over the past few weeks, and I think that trend continues. Henry has rushed for under 60 yards in four consecutive games. C hargers force three turnovers The Ravens will have yet another quarterback under center: veteran Jacoby Brissett. The Chargers' defense has been the team's only bright spot. Their offense and defense haven't provided enough complementary football this season, but forcing turnovers could help change that. Brissett has had a mixed -to-rough time taking care of the football this season. Los Angeles will take care of that. Justin Herbert has his best game of the season on primetime Justin Herbert is playing the worst football of his NFL career. He's coming off another disappointing performance against Houston, throwing for 193 yards and one touchdown in a 44-22 loss. However, Herbert has a chance to play his best game yet against an inconsistent Ravens defense. Baltimore is allowing 329.7 passing yards per game, and while Herbert has yet to reach 300+ passing yards, that will happen in front of a national audience. away.headline: Chargers Issue Big Update on Ladd McConkey’s Status for Monday’s Game vs. Ravens
away.blurb: McConkey had been listed as questionable on Saturday. But on Sunday, the team downgraded his status to out. This has been a rough season for him in more ways than one. Health-wise, he has been dinged up, as he has dealt with cracked ribs, a foot injury, a concussion in addition to the back spasms that kept him out of action last week. Njoku could've helped out in that regard, but he suffered a knee injury in Week 2 versus the Las Vegas Raiders and has been out since. L.A.'s running game hasn't been able to pick up the slack, as running back Omarion Hampton's production has fallen after a promising rookie campaign last year. Three Key Offensive Players Could Return for Chargers on Monday Versus Ravens Chargers Issue Big Update on Ladd McConkey’s Status for Monday’s Game vs. Ravens - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL College football winners/losers Robert Marvi · Athlon Sports Mon, November 16, 2026 at 2:28 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The 0-8 Los Angeles Chargers are still searching for their first win since last December, and they will head to Maryland for a Monday Night Football game against the Baltimore Ravens as they look to end their losing streak. They could get offensive linemen Kayode Awosika and Trey Pipkins III and tight end David Njoku back on Monday . They had also been hoping that wide receiver Ladd McConkey will be able to take the field after missing last Sunday's loss to the Houston Texans due to a back ailment. Unfortunately, Los Angeles will have to go to war again without McConkey. Last season, McConkey had a decent 66 catches for 789 yards and six touchdowns. But so far this season, he's at just 17 catches, 286 yards and one touchdown in six games. One of the many reasons the Chargers came into Week 10 ranked last in scoring is their lack of pass-catching threats. Wide receiver Quentin Johnston, a first-round draft pick in 2023, has never become the consistent deep threat some thought he would be when he came into the NFL. Baltimore is a weak defensive team, so the hope is that L.A.'s offense will be able to find enough holes to look at least somewhat competent. But there is little hope in that regard, given how incompetent and disjointed that offense has been all year. In addition to ranking last in scoring, the Chargers were also last in turnovers coming into this week. away.headline: Move Over Substation, Chargers Have a New King of Injuries in LA with Week 10 Report
away.blurb: Move Over Substation, Chargers Have a New King of Injuries in LA with Week 10 Report Skip to main content SI.COM The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-8, they just had a final hour trade before the trade deadline fall through and they are still searching for any sort of identity on offense. Los Angeles has been dealing with injuries all season long, by Week Six they already had over half of their original 53-man roster on the injury report or injured reserve. The Chargers injury luck is not improving much. For all the jokes and talk about the electrical substation near the San Francisco 49ers practice facility, Los Angeles may have something worse. The Chargers' practice facility, the Bolt, is located near Los Angeles International Airport, perhaps it's the air quality, or something in the the Los Angeles water or perhaps SoFi Stadium itself, something is up in LA. The Rams, who now have placed another wide receiver on injured reserve, may agree SoFi stadium, the Chargers and Rams' shared stadium, has a role in this. Both Los Angeles teams are in the top 10 of most injured this season in nearly every metric. The Chargers emerge from the NFL trade deadline with the exact same roster and will now head to Baltimore to take on the Jacoby Brissett-led Ravens on Monday Night Football. The Chargers will have a chance to steal their first win of the season as the Ravens search for their identity with a brand new quarterback at the helm but will their long list of injuries get in the way? thursday's injury report for week 10 at BAL pic.twitter.com/fXSvi1MmEt It feels like groundhog day for the Chargers and their MASH unit of players following their loss to the Houston Texans. The Chargers have a significant portion of their cornerback room on the injury report. Tarheeb Still and Donte Jackson are the only cornerbacks not on the injury report to start the week of practice. The Chargers offensive line continues to be cursed. Guards Kayode Awosika, Alex Harkey and Branson Taylor are all on the injury report and Taylor was unable to practice at all after getting his first snaps of the season against Houston. Wide receivers Ladd McConkey and Tre' Harris are both on the report with McConkey missing the first practice of the week following suffering back spasms during pregame warmups prior to the week nine matchup against the Texans. The Chargers have had a revolving door at most positions on offense this season, which certainly has not helped their performance. As the Chargers, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel and quarterback Justin Herbert continue to try to dial in the offense, their efforts are clearly made more of a challenge with the amount of injuries facing the unit.
