home.headline: Ravens’ Jesse Minter addresses statement on Lamar Jackson: ‘Same page’
home.blurb: Rookie running back Adam Randall (neck/hamstring), who has yet to be activated from injured reserve, and safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) were the only players on the final injury report ahead of Monday night’s game against the Los Angeles Chargers at M&T Bank Stadium. Randall is listed as questionable, while Hawkins was ruled out. Jackson underwent surgery to repair the broken and dislocated right thumb on his throwing hand, Minter said Friday in a statement after declining to discuss the matter earlier in the week. Asked on Saturday what prompted him to make a statement, he said he wanted to “get it out there” so that there was “less speculation” about the injury and a timeline for a possible return. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey, who has dealt with a slew of injuries, including a back injury that kept him out of last week’s game against the Houston Texans, was listed as questionable after being limited in practice Saturday. It was his first practice of the week. Also questionable are starting left guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), starting defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe (ankle), rotational linebacker Denzel Perryman (pectoral), tight end David Njoku (fibula) and offensive lineman Trey Pipkins III (knee). Wide receiver Brenen Thompson (hamstring) is listed as doubtful, while cornerback Isas Waxter (ankle), safety Kendall Williamson (calf) and offensive lineman Branson Taylor (ankle) are all out. A few extra days off proved beneficial to the Ravens. Hawkins, who signed a two-year, $10 million free agent deal with Baltimore this offseason but has largely struggled even when healthy, hasn’t played since a Week 6 loss to the Browns in Cleveland. Baltimore has until 4 p.m. Saturday to activate Randall for this week’s game and until Wednesday to activate him or he would revert to season-ending injured reserve. The Ravens (4-5) are looking to break a four-game losing streak, while the Chargers (0-8) are looking for their first win of the season. “[We] had a really good week,” Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Saturday. “It’s about taking preparation to the field now.” That preparation, of course, included breaking in the fourth different starting quarterback this season. Baltimore acquired veteran Jacoby Brissett in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals last week, and he will start against the Chargers and for the foreseeable future. The move came after Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler “Snoop” Huntley were both injured in a Week 8 loss to the Buffalo Bills , forcing undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into duty for the rest of that game and into his first NFL start four days later against the Jacksonville Jaguars. home.headline: New Lamar Jackson Rumors Update When Ravens QB Had Surgery amid Latest Injury Timeline for Return
home.blurb: Baltimore Ravens star quarterback Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this season based on when he had thumb surgery. "He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return," Minter said. "We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season." Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , Jackson's surgery happened last week so based on the estimated recovery time of six to 10 weeks, he could potentially be back on the field before the regular season ends. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said in a statement on Nov. 13 that Jackson's recovery timeline was "challenging to predict" after he underwent surgery to address a dislocated and broken right thumb. A six-week recovery would have Jackson back around Week 15 when the Ravens play the Pittsburgh Steelers. The full 10-week timeline would give him a chance to play in Week 18, also against the Steelers. In addition to his hand injury, Jackson also missed three games earlier in the year after suffering a high ankle sprain. In five games, he played just 14 full quarters and threw for 961 yards, six touchdowns and one interception while adding 144 rushing yards and another score. In the wake of Jackson's injury, the Ravens traded for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who is expected to make his first start for the team against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football in Week 10. At 4-5, Baltimore has work to do if it hopes to make the playoffs. The Ravens will likely remain cautious with Jackson's recovery, making the acquisition of Brissett a critical move as they look to snap their four-game losing streak going into Monday night.

home.headline: Ravens reveal Lamar Jackson injury timeline that might not end his season
home.blurb: Huntley is out for the remainder of the 2026 NFL season, and Jackson's injury was also seen as season-ending. But ahead of Week 10, the Ravens shared some big news. The 5-4 Ravens will need a lot of things to go their way, including Jackson's recovery going well. But even if it takes the full 10 weeks, as Minter revealed in the statement, Jackson could return in the first round of the playoffs, or in Week 18. There is still a lot of uncertainty when it comes to Jackson returning for the Ravens, but just hearing that he has a chance to return at some point this season, after the doom and gloom a few weeks ago, is some very positive news for the Ravens. home.headline: Chargers Issue Big Update on Ladd McConkey’s Status for Monday’s Game vs. Ravens
home.blurb: McConkey had been listed as questionable on Saturday. But on Sunday, the team downgraded his status to out. This has been a rough season for him in more ways than one. Health-wise, he has been dinged up, as he has dealt with cracked ribs, a foot injury, a concussion in addition to the back spasms that kept him out of action last week. Njoku could've helped out in that regard, but he suffered a knee injury in Week 2 versus the Las Vegas Raiders and has been out since. L.A.'s running game hasn't been able to pick up the slack, as running back Omarion Hampton's production has fallen after a promising rookie campaign last year. They could get offensive linemen Kayode Awosika and Trey Pipkins III and tight end David Njoku back on Monday . They had also been hoping that wide receiver Ladd McConkey will be able to take the field after missing last Sunday's loss to the Houston Texans due to a back ailment. Unfortunately, Los Angeles will have to go to war again without McConkey. Last season, McConkey had a decent 66 catches for 789 yards and six touchdowns. But so far this season, he's at just 17 catches, 286 yards and one touchdown in six games. One of the many reasons the Chargers came into Week 10 ranked last in scoring is their lack of pass-catching threats. Wide receiver Quentin Johnston, a first-round draft pick in 2023, has never become the consistent deep threat some thought he would be when he came into the NFL. Baltimore is a weak defensive team, so the hope is that L.A.'s offense will be able to find enough holes to look at least somewhat competent. But there is little hope in that regard, given how incompetent and disjointed that offense has been all year. In addition to ranking last in scoring, the Chargers were also last in turnovers coming into this week.
